From that day on, John made sure to keep a closer eye on all his animals so they wouldn't wander off again.

Finally, he saw a shiny metal piece that was the perfect size. He grabbed it and scampered back to the broken toy. He put the piece in place and the toy was fixed!

He was so happy, he jumped up and down and shouted, "I fixed it!" Everyone on the beach was so proud of him and they cheered.

The busy crab was glad that he had fixed the toy. He was so proud of himself!

The brother and sister did their sorting together. They sorted out all the toys and both of them were very happy. They hugged each other and smiled. They had worked together to sort all the toys and it made them both very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful zebra. She loved to gallop around the field and tasted the sweet grass. One day, she was running around the field when she looked up and saw an amazing sight. It was a lion! The lion let out a loud roar. The zebra was scared and ran away to the other side of the field.

The lion followed the zebra and kept roaring. Suddenly, the zebra stopped and looked back at the lion. She was curious and not scared anymore. The lion saw the zebra and stopped roaring. He walked slowly towards her and the zebra didn't move.

The lion and the zebra stood there looking at each other. After a while, the lion became friends with the zebra. From that day on, the lion and the zebra were best pals. They roamed around the field together and had lots of fun.  The lion never roared again and the zebra was no longer scared. They were a beautiful pair of friends. The End.

Tim said, "Yes, I would love to go with you!" So, Lily and Tim walked together to the east side of town. They talked, laughed, and played with Lily's toys. They had a fun day and became good friends.

At the end of the day, the sun began to set. Lily and Tim were tired from their adventure. They decided to go back to their homes. As they said goodbye, Lily gave Tim one of her toys to remember their fun day together.

From that day on, Lily and Tim would often meet and play together. They had many more adventures, and their friendship grew stronger. And Lily always remembered to carry her toys with her, just in case she met another friend along the way.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim lived in a nest made of sticks and wire. The wire was shiny and strong. It held the nest together so it would not fall apart.

One day, Tim saw a big cat with a serious face. The cat was looking at Tim's nest. Tim was scared. He did not want the cat to eat him. So, Tim decided to frown at the cat. He put on his best frown and hoped the cat would go away.

The cat saw Tim's frown and felt sad. The cat did not want to make Tim upset. So, the cat walked away. Tim was happy that his frown worked. He knew that his nest was safe, and he could live happily with the shiny wire holding it together.

"Can I pour the batter into the pan, mom?" Sara asked.

"Not yet, honey. We need to add some chocolate chips. They will make the cake even better," mom said.

She gave Sara a handful of chocolate chips. Sara sprinkled them over the batter. They looked like little brown dots.

"Can I pour the batter into the pan now, mom?" Sara asked.

"Yes, honey. You can do it. But be very careful. The pan is hot," mom said.

She helped Sara lift the bowl and pour the batter into the pan. Sara was very proud. She had made a cake for dad.

"Good job, honey. You are a great helper. Now we have to put the cake in the oven and wait for it to bake," mom said.

She hugged Sara and kissed her cheek. Sara hugged her back and said, "I love you, mom. And I love your lovely apron."

Sara was sad. She missed her mom. Mom went to work and Sara stayed with grandma. Grandma was nice, but Sara wanted mom.

Grandma saw Sara crying. She hugged Sara and said, "Don't cry, my dear. Mom will come back soon. She loves you very much. She works hard to make you happy."

Sara sniffed and said, "But I miss her. I want to see her."

Mom, Sara, and grandma smiled and cuddled. They were a happy family.

"Kite, kite, come back!" Tom called. "I'm sorry I left you!"

But the kite did not hear him. It soared higher and higher, until it was a tiny dot in the sky. Tom ran after it, but he could not catch it. He wished he had kept his kite and let the cricket go. "Hello, bee," she whispered. "What are you doing?"

The bee heard her and flew closer to her. Lily held her breath and hoped the bee would be nice.

"I'm looking for nectar," the bee said. "Nectar is a sweet juice that flowers make. I take it back to my hive and make honey. Honey is good for me and my friends."

"That sounds fun," Lily said. "Can I see your hive?"

"Sure, if you want," the bee said. "But you have to be careful. There are many bees in my hive and they might not like you. You have to be quiet and gentle and not touch anything."

"OK, I will," Lily said. "Can I polish your wings? They look a little dusty."

The bee laughed. "No, thank you. My wings are fine. They are not like your shoes. They don't need wax or cloth. They need air and sun and water. But you can polish this flower if you like. It is green and pretty and smells nice."

Lily smiled and took her cloth and wax. She rubbed the wax on the green flower and then made it shiny with the cloth. The flower looked brighter and happier. "Tom, give me back Anna!" Lily cried. She chased Tom around the house. Tom laughed and teased her. He threw Anna in the air and caught her. He pulled her hair and twisted her arms. He made her say funny things. "I am Anna, and I am stupid. I don't like Lily, I like Tom. He is the best, and I am the worst."

Lily was very sad and angry. She wanted to stop Tom, but he was faster and stronger. She felt like crying. She wished Anna could talk to her and comfort her. She wished Anna could be real and have magic.

Suddenly, something strange happened. Anna glowed with a bright light. She slipped from Tom's hands and fell on the floor. She stood up and looked at Tom and Lily. She smiled at Lily and frowned at Tom. She spoke with a sweet voice. "Lily, I am here. I am real and I have magic. You are my best friend, and I love you. Tom, you are mean and rude. You hurt me and Lily. You need to say sorry and be nice."

Tom and Lily were shocked. They could not believe their eyes and ears. Anna was alive and had magic. How did this happen? Anna explained. "Lily, you wished for me to be real and have magic. Your wish was so strong and pure that it came true. You restored me with your love. You gave me a gift, and I want to give you a gift too. I can share my magic with you. We can play together and have fun. But we have to be careful and kind. Magic is powerful and precious. We have to use it for good and not for bad."

Lily was overjoyed. She hugged Anna and thanked her. She was sorry for Tom, too. She knew he was lonely and bored. She wanted to share her magic and her dolls with him. She asked Anna if they could do that. Anna agreed. She said she was willing to forgive Tom if he was sorry and nice. She looked at Tom and waited for his answer.

Tom was scared and ashamed. He realized he was wrong and mean. He hurt Lily and Anna. He did not want to lose his sister and her magic. He wanted to be friends with them. He said sorry to Lily and Anna. He asked them if they could play with him. He said he would be nice and gentle. He said he liked dolls and magic.

Lily and Anna smiled. They accepted Tom's apology and invitation. They gave him a doll and a magic wand. They taught him how to play and use magic. They had a lot of fun. They became a happy and charming trio. They learned to share and care. They lived in a world of magic and love.

Annabelle felt relieved. She had not expected to find a friend in this quiet lane.
"Yes," said Annabelle. "I'm just settling here for the night. It gets a bit too busy in the traffic."
Jane smiled.
"Let's be friends," she said.
And so Annabelle and Jane were the best of friends. They would spend their days together, away from the noise of the traffic, settling in the quiet lane.

So, Jo got some food for Jim and served it to him every day. Jo also made sure to give Jim some fresh water each day. After some time, Jim got healthier and his feathers started getting brighter.

Jo had learned a valuable lesson that day - taking care of your things is very important, no matter how busy you are.

Once upon a time there was a pear tree that was always full of delicious pears. Every morning, the sun shined brightly on the delicious pears. One day, Lucy saw the pears and decided she wanted one. She went up to the tree and stretched up as high as she could to get one of the pears, but she couldn't reach. 

Then, a kind old lady saw her and said, "That tree is not ours. We must never take things that don't belong to us". Lucy listened and said, "Ok, I won't take it". 

The old lady showed Lucy how to ask for things nicely. She said, "If you want something from someone, you must always ask politely". Lucy nodded and went home. 

The next day, Lucy's mom went to the shop and asked if she could buy some of the delicious pears. The shopkeeper said "yes". Lucy and her mom took the pears home. 

This story teaches us that it is important to ask for things politely. We should never take things that don't belong to us.

Tommy was a selfish boy. He never wanted to share with his friends. One Wednesday, his teacher told the class they were going on a field trip. Everyone was so excited, except Tommy. He wasn't excited because he knew he wouldn't get to be the first one to do everything.

His teacher noticed Tommy's reluctance. She asked, "Tommy, why aren't you as excited as the rest of the kids? Is there something you don't know about the trip?"

Tommy looked down and said, "No, I know what it is."

His teacher looked at him suspiciously and said, "Are you sure? If there's something you don't know, it's okay to tell me."

But Tommy was too selfish to share his thoughts. He didn't want anyone else to get the chance to do something he wanted to do. He shook his head and said, "No, I'm okay."

Unfortunately, on the day of the field trip, it started raining. Everyone would've had a great time at the field trip, but because of Tommy's selfishness, they all had to stay inside, and their fun was completely ruined.

The other friend thought for a moment, then he said, "No, it's not a good idea to touch it. You should just be careful and admire it from afar." 

The one friend nodded again and he smiled. He then turned to his friend and said, "Let's go over there and find something else to do."

The other friend grinned and said, "Yes it is. Let's rub it gently and see how it feels."

So the one friend rubbed the butterfly ever so softly and the butterfly fluttered away. 

The two friends looked at each other and smiled, happy that the butterfly was safe. At the same time, they learned a valuable lesson: it is best to admire all creatures from afar, rather than touching them.

They did not know that the smoke would make the alarm beep. They did not know that mom would come home and see the mess.

Mom was very surprised and scared when she saw the kitchen. She saw the smoke and the alarm and the cake. She saw Tom and Lily with flour and sugar on their faces and clothes. She was glad that they were not hurt, but she was also angry and sad. She asked them what they were doing and why they did not ask for help. They tried to explain that they wanted to make a cake for her, but they did not know the words or the measures. They showed her the book and pointed at the picture.

She said that the measures were important and they could not guess them. She said that the words were helpful and they could ask her to read them. She said that she appreciated their gift, but they had to clean up the kitchen. She said that they could make a cake together another day, but first they had to learn some words and measures. Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the farm. They had a dog named Spot and a cat named Fluff. One day, their dad said he had to send some wheat to the mill. He asked Ben and Lily if they wanted to go with him.

"Yes, yes, yes!" they said. They loved to see the big machines that turned the wheat into flour. They got into the truck with their dad and Spot. Fluff stayed at home to nap.

When they got to the mill, they saw a man with a long beard and a hat. He was the miller. He smiled and said hello to them.

"Hello, Mr. Miller," their dad said. "I have some wheat for you. Can you make it into flour for me?"

"Sure, I can," the miller said. "But you have to answer a riddle first. If you answer right, I will make your flour for free. If you answer wrong, you have to pay me double. Do you want to play?"

Their dad thought for a moment. He liked riddles, but he was not very good at them. He looked at Ben and Lily. They looked excited and curious.

"OK, I will play," their dad said. "What is your riddle?"

The miller said, "What is always coming but never arrives?"

Their dad scratched his head. He could not think of anything. He looked at Ben and Lily. They whispered to each other. Then, Lily raised her hand.

"I know, I know!" she said. "Can I say it?"

The miller nodded. He was surprised that a little girl knew the answer.

Lily said, "The answer is tomorrow. Tomorrow is always coming but never arrives."

The miller clapped his hands. He was impressed by Lily's answer.

"That is right, that is right!" he said. "You are a very wise girl. You have solved my riddle. I will make your flour for free. You can come and watch if you want."

Ben and Lily cheered. They hugged their dad and thanked him for taking them to the mill. They followed the miller and saw how he poured the wheat into a big hopper. Then, they heard a loud noise as the wheat was crushed by the stones. They saw the flour come out of a pipe and fill a bag. They smelled the fresh and sweet aroma of the flour.

They had a lot of fun at the mill. They learned something new and made a new friend. They thanked the miller and took their flour home. They gave some to their mom, who baked them a cake. They shared the cake with Spot and Fluff. They were happy and full. They went to bed and dreamed of tomorrow.

He would catch his dinner soon, he just knew it. So he curled up to rest his head and waited patiently for the moon to rise.

Tim put on his old sweater and started to spray the blue color. He sprayed and sprayed until the whole sweater was blue. But, Tim did not stop there. He sprayed the color on the floor and on the walls too.

When his mom saw the mess, she was not happy. She said, "Tim, you have spoiled the room with the blue color." Tim felt sad and said, "I am sorry, mom."

His mom said, "It's okay, Tim. We can clean it together." So, Tim and his mom cleaned the room and the walls. Tim learned to be careful when playing with colors. And, he loved his new blue sweater.

Once upon a time, in a far away land, there was a big gem. This gem was very lonely. It was all by itself in a dark cave. One day, a little boy found the gem. The boy was happy to have a new friend. He played with the gem all day long.

The boy did not want to forget his new friend, the gem. So, he took the gem everywhere he went. They played in the park, they went to the store, and they even ate lunch together. The gem was not lonely anymore. It was happy to be with the boy.

The gem was all alone again, feeling sad and lonely. The boy was very upset when he realized his mistake. He went back to the beach to find the gem, but it was gone. The boy had lost his friend forever. The moral of the story is to always take care of your friends and not to forget them.

Tom cried out, "Help, help!" But no one could hear him over the sound of the rain and the train. The train got closer and closer, and finally, it reached Tom and Tim.

Sadly, Tom and Tim couldn't get away in time. The train went by, and they were gone. The rain kept falling, and the town was very sad to lose their furry friend and little bird.

The witch told the little girl to go into the dark forest and find a special flower. The little girl was scared, but she did what the witch said. She went into the forest and found the flower. When she came back, the witch took the flower and smiled.

But the witch did not keep her promise. She did not help the little girl find her way home. The little girl was very sad and cried. The witch laughed and went back into her now comfortable house, leaving the little girl all alone in the dark forest.

Tom walked around with the key. He saw a tree with a big hole. He thought, "Maybe the key can open the tree." He put the key in the hole and turned it. The tree opened like a door. Inside the tree, there were many flowers.

Tom saw a flower that he liked. He wanted to take the flower home. So, he took a small tool to cut the flower. He cut the flower carefully and put it in his bag. Then, he closed the tree door with the big key.

Tom walked back home with the flower and the key. He showed his mom the flower and the key. His mom was happy to see them. They put the flower in a vase and the key on a hook. Tom felt good that he found the big key and the pretty flower.

Sue found a long string in her room. She thought it would be perfect to attach to her book. Sue tied one end of the string to her book and the other end to her bag. Now, she was sure she would never lose her book.

One day, Sue went to the park with her mom. She played on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. She had so much fun that she forgot about her book. When it was time to go home, Sue suddenly remembered her book. She looked at her bag and saw the string. She followed the string and found her book in the sandbox. Sue was so happy that her idea worked. From that day on, Sue always attached her book to her bag and never lost it again.

One day, their mom told them that they had to sell some of their old toys to make room for new ones. She gave them a big box and told them to put the toys they did not want inside.

Tom and Lily looked at their toys and felt sad. They did not want to sell any of them. They loved all their toys, even the ones they did not play with much. They tried to hide some of their toys under the bed, in the closet, and behind the curtains. But their mom found them and put them back in the box.

"Please, mom, can we keep our toys?" Tom and Lily begged.

"No, sweeties, you have too many toys. You have to share with other kids who do not have any. It will make them happy, and you will have more space for new toys," their mom said.

"But we do not want new toys. We want our old toys. They are our friends," Tom and Lily said.

Their mom sighed and hugged them. She understood how they felt, but she also wanted them to learn to let go of things they did not need. She had an idea.

"How about this? You can keep one toy each from the box, and the rest we will sell. And with the money we get, we will buy a new bathtub toy that you can both play with. How does that sound?" she asked.

Tom and Lily thought about it. They looked at the box and picked one toy each that they liked the most. Tom chose a rubber duck, and Lily chose a plastic fish. They gave the rest of the toys to their mom, who smiled and thanked them.

"Good job, kids. You are very kind and generous. Now, let's go to the store and see what bathtub toy we can find," she said.

Tom and Lily felt a little better. They still missed their old toys, but they were also curious about the new one. They hoped it would be fun and jolly, like their old ones. They held their mom's hand and walked to the store.

They always asked for more and more, and they never shared with each other or their friends. They were spoiled children.

One day, their mom and dad brought home a big box. They said it was a surprise for Anna and Ben, and they had to wait until the next day to open it. Anna and Ben were very curious and excited. They wondered what was inside the box. Maybe it was a new bike, or a dollhouse, or a robot. They could not wait to see.

That night, when their mom and dad were asleep, Anna and Ben sneaked into the living room. They saw the big box on the table. They decided to peek inside and see what was the surprise. They used a scissors to cut the tape and opened the box. They were shocked by what they saw. Inside the box, there was no toy, but a lot of wires and metal pieces. They looked like parts of a machine, but they did not know what it was.

"What is this?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. It looks boring and ugly," Ben said.

"Maybe it's a mistake. Maybe mom and dad got the wrong box," Anna said.

"Or maybe they are trying to trick us. Maybe they don't love us anymore," Ben said.

They felt angry and sad. They threw the wires and metal pieces out of the box and onto the floor. They made a big mess. They did not care. They wanted a toy, not a junk.

The next morning, their mom and dad came into the living room. They saw the big box opened and the wires and metal pieces scattered all over the floor. They also saw Anna and Ben sitting on the couch, looking unhappy.

"What happened here?" their mom asked.

"Who did this?" their dad asked.

Anna and Ben did not answer. They looked down and felt ashamed.

Their mom and dad sighed. They said, "We are very disappointed in you, Anna and Ben. You did not listen to us. You did not wait for the surprise. You did not respect our gift. You did not appreciate our love."

They explained that the wires and metal pieces were not junk, but parts of a special toy. They said that they had bought a kit to build a toy car with Anna and Ben. They said that they wanted to spend time with them and teach them how to make something with their own hands. They said that they wanted to give them a fun and educational experience, not just a toy. They said that they wanted to reveal the surprise together, and see their happy faces.

They said, "But you ruined the surprise. You spoiled the fun. You wasted the opportunity. You hurt our feelings."

Anna and Ben realized that they had made a big mistake. They felt sorry and guilty. They said, "We are sorry, mom and dad. We were wrong. We were selfish. We were spoiled. We did not know what you had planned for us. We did not think about your hard work and your love. We only thought about ourselves. We are sorry. Please forgive us."

Their mom and dad hugged them and said, "We forgive you, Anna and Ben. We love you, no matter what. But we hope you learned a lesson. We hope you learned to be patient, to be grateful, to be curious, to be creative, to be respectful, and to be loving. We hope you learned that the best gifts are not always the ones that you can see, but the ones that you can share."

They helped them clean up the mess and put the wires and metal pieces back into the box. They said, "Maybe we can still build the toy car together, if you want. Maybe we can still have some fun and learn something new. Maybe we can still enjoy the surprise, even if it's not a surprise anymore."

Anna and Ben nodded and smiled. They said, "Yes, please. We want to build the toy car with you. We want to have fun and learn something new. We want to enjoy the surprise, even if it's not a surprise anymore. We want to share the gift with you. We love you, mom and dad. Thank you for the gift."

"Easy," Max said. "You just make a big cone and put a stick on top. Like this." He started to scoop sand with his shovel.

Lily watched him for a while. She did not think his rocket looked very good. It was just a pile of sand with a stick. She wanted him to play with her castle.

"Max, come and play with me," she said. "My castle is better. It has a flag and a door. And it looks like a real castle."

"No, Lily, I want to play with my rocket," Max said. "My rocket is better. It can fly to the moon and the stars. And it looks like a real rocket."

They argued for a while. Lily insisted that her castle was better. Max insisted that his rocket was better. They did not want to play with each other's sand creations.

"Hey, stop that!" Lily and Max shouted. "That's our sand! That's our castle and our rocket!"

But the dog did not listen. It ruined their sand creations. It knocked down the tower and the flag. It bit the stick and the cone. It made a big mess.

Lily and Max were very sad. They looked at their sand creations. They were not castles or rockets anymore. They were just ordinary sand.

They looked at each other. They felt sorry for each other. They decided to stop arguing and start playing together.

"Let's make a new sand creation," Lily said. "Something we both like."

"OK, Lily," Max said. "What do you want to make?"

"Let's make a cake," Lily said. "A big cake with sand and sticks. And we can pretend to eat it."

"OK, Lily," Max said. "That sounds fun. Let's make a cake."

They smiled and hugged. They took their bucket and shovel and started to make a cake. They forgot about the dog and the sand. They were happy.

They play happily for a while. Then they hear a loud noise. It is a big dog. The dog runs towards them. It barks and growls. It wants the toys.

"Help, help!" Tom and Mia say. They are scared of the dog. They drop the toys and run away. The dog chases them.

They see a big tree. They run to the tree. They climb up the tree. They are safe.

"Phew, that was close!" Tom says. "Are you OK, Mia?"

"Yes, I'm OK, Tom. But what about the toys?" Mia says. "The dog took them all."

They look down. They see the dog. The dog has the toys in its mouth. It shakes them and tears them. It makes a big mess.

"That's not fair!" Tom and Mia say. "The dog is not sharing. The dog is mean."

They are sad. They want their toys back. But they can't get them. The dog is too big and strong.

They sit on the tree. They wait for the dog to go away. They hope someone will come and help them. They hug each other. They are still friends. They share their feelings. They are not alone.

One day, he is writing a poem about his cat. He writes: "My cat is black and white. He likes to play and bite. He sleeps on my bed at night. He is my best friend, all right." He smiles and looks for another crayon.

But then, his big brother Tom comes in. Tom is enormous. He is much bigger than Ben. He sees Ben's paper and crayons. He wants to play with them. He grabs them from Ben and says: "What is this? This is not a poem. This is silly. I can write a better poem."

Ben is very angry. He says: "No, Tom, give them back. That is my poem. You are disturbing me. You are mean." He tries to get his paper and crayons back, but Tom is too strong. He pushes Ben away and laughs.

Ben starts to cry. He runs to his mom and tells her what Tom did. Mom is not happy. She goes to Tom's room and scolds him. She says: "Tom, you should not disturb your brother. You should not take his things. You should not make fun of his poems. You should say sorry to him and give him back his paper and crayons."

Tom feels bad. He knows he was wrong. He says sorry to Ben and gives him back his paper and crayons. He says: "Your poem is nice. I like your cat. Can I write a poem with you?" Ben smiles and says: "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice and share." They hug and write poems together. Mom is happy. She says: "That's better. You are good brothers." She gives them cookies and milk. They eat and drink and write more poems. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to whistle all day long. He would whistle when he played, when he ate, and even when he slept.

One sunny day, Tim went for a walk near the creek. He saw a frog sitting on a rock. The frog was green and slimy. Tim thought the frog looked disgusting. He did not want to play with the frog. Instead, he started to whistle a happy song.

The frog heard Tim's whistle and started to dance. Tim was surprised and smiled. He played with the frog, and they became good friends. The frog taught Tim that even if something looks disgusting, it can still be fun and kind.

From that day on, Tim learned not to judge others by how they look. He and the frog played together by the creek every day, whistling and dancing in the sun. And they lived happily ever after.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge a book by its cover.

"No, Tim, it's too high and too fast. I don't want to go on the slide." Lily says.

"Are you afraid, Lily? I dare you to go on the slide with me. It will be fun, I promise." Tim says.

Lily thinks for a moment. She doesn't want to be afraid, but she also doesn't want to get hurt. She looks at the slide and sees that it has a rubber mat at the end. Maybe that will make it softer and safer.

"Okay, Tim, I will go on the slide with you. But you have to hold my hand." Lily says.

"Okay, Lily, I will hold your hand. Don't worry, we will be fine." Tim says.

They climb up the stairs and sit on the slide. Tim holds Lily's hand and counts to three. Then they slide down together, feeling the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laugh and scream as they reach the bottom and land on the rubber mat.

"Wow, that was fun!" Tim says.

"Yes, it was fun! You were right, Tim. The rubber mat made it soft and safe." Lily says.

They hug each other and smile. They are happy and proud. They have tried something new and overcome their fear. They have also learned a new word: dare.

"Say more, say more!" they said.

Coco said, "OK, I will. But first, you have to do something for me. You have to take me out of this tree and bring me to your home. I don't like this tree. It is too small and boring. I want to see more things and have more fun. Will you do that for me?"

"I don't know, Coco," Lily said. "We are not allowed to take you. You belong to someone else. Maybe they will miss you."

Lily and Tom felt sorry for Coco. They thought he was very sad and lonely. They wanted to make him happy. They decided to take him with them.

"OK, Coco," Tom said. "We will take you with us. But you have to be quiet and hide in our backpack. We don't want anyone to see you or hear you. Do you understand?"

Coco nodded and said, "Yes, I understand. Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are the best. I love you."

I hate you. I will hurt you. I will escape and fly away. You are stupid and foolish. You should have listened to your mom and dad. They know better than you. Now you will pay for your mistake."

The end.

Lila was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new places. One day, she found a shiny bottle in her mom's closet. She opened it and saw a purple liquid inside. She was curious and smelled it. It smelled like candy. She wanted to taste it, but then she heard her mom calling her name.

"Lila, where are you? It's time for lunch!"

Lila quickly put the bottle in her pocket and ran to the kitchen. She sat down and ate her sandwich and apple. She was still thinking about the purple liquid. She wondered what it would do. She decided to try it after lunch, when her mom was busy.

She finished her food and said, "Mom, can I play in my room?"

"Sure, honey, but don't make a mess, okay?"

"Okay, mom, I won't."

Lila ran to her room and closed the door. She took out the bottle and looked at it. She opened it again and poured a little bit on her tongue. It tasted sweet and sour. She liked it. She drank some more. She felt funny. She looked at her hands. They were smaller. She looked at her feet. They were smaller too. She was shrinking!

She dropped the bottle and screamed. "Mom, help! I'm shrinking!"

She heard her mom's footsteps. She tried to run to the door, but it was too far. She saw a wall. She ran to the wall and climbed on it. She hoped her mom would see her.

"Mom, I'm here! On the wall!"

Her mom opened the door and looked around. She saw the bottle on the floor and the purple liquid spilled. She saw Lila on the wall, tiny and scared.

"Lila, what did you do? How did you shrink?"

"Mom, I'm sorry, I drank the purple liquid. It was in your closet. It smelled like candy. I didn't know it would make me shrink. Please, make me big again!"

Her mom picked up the bottle and read the label. It said, "Shrink potion. Do not drink. To reverse the effect, drink water."

Her mom grabbed a glass of water and poured some on Lila. Lila felt a tingling sensation. She started to grow. She grew bigger and bigger until she was back to her normal size. She hugged her mom and cried.

"Mom, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I won't be adventurous again. I won't touch your things again. I love you, mom."

Her mom hugged her back and kissed her. She said, "I love you too, Lila. I'm glad you're okay. But you have to be careful, honey. Some things are not for children. Some things are dangerous. You have to ask me before you try anything new, okay?"

"Okay, mom, I will. I promise."

Her mom smiled and said, "Now, let's clean up this mess and then we can have some cookies and milk, okay?"

"Okay, mom, that sounds good."

Lila and her mom cleaned up the room and threw away the bottle. They went to the kitchen and had some cookies and milk. Lila learned her lesson. She was still adventurous, but she was also more careful. She never drank anything strange again.

Lily saw the bee too. She knew it was not a pretty thing. She knew it was a bad thing. She had seen a bee sting her mom once. It made her mom cry and say ouch. She did not want Tim to get stung. She said, "No, Tim, no! That is a bee! It can hurt you! Come away!"

But Tim did not listen. He was too curious. He touched the bee. The bee did not like it. It got angry. It stung Tim on his finger. Tim felt a sharp pain. He screamed and dropped the bee. He ran to Lily and showed her his finger. It was red and swollen. He said, "Ow, ow, ow! It bit me! It bit me!"

Lily felt sorry for Tim. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I tried to warn you. It did not bite you. It stung you. That is what bees do when they are scared or mad. You have to be careful with bees. They are not toys. They are alive."

Tim was still crying. He did not understand why the bee stung him. He did not mean to hurt it. He just wanted to see it. He said, "But it was so pretty. It was yellow like the sun. Why did it sting me?"

Lily said, "Because it was not a sun. It was a bee. And bees have stingers. They use them to protect themselves. They do not like to be touched. They like to be left alone. Next time, you have to look but not touch. Okay?"

Tim nodded. He learned his lesson. He did not want to touch a bee again. He said, "Okay. I'm sorry, bee. I won't touch you again. Can you forgive me?"

The bee did not answer. It flew away. It was hurt too. It had lost its stinger. It could not sting again. It had to find a new home. It was sad.

The owl told the bird to bathe in the river every day for a week. The little bird followed the owl's advice and after a week, he was able to fly again. The moral of the story was that sometimes we need to do things that may seem strange or difficult to solve our problems.

Lily listened carefully to the story and asked her grandma, "Can I bathe in the river too?" Her grandma smiled and said, "Sure, but always ask for help from a grown-up first." Lily nodded and went to bed with a happy heart, knowing that she had learned something new. From that day on, she always remembered the story of the little bird and the wise old owl.

One day, they decided to play a game with the curtain. Lily said, "I will say a word, and you have to repeat it. If you say it wrong, you lose." Ben agreed, and they took turns hiding behind the curtain and saying words.

Lily said, "Cat." Ben repeated, "Cat." Lily said, "Dog." Ben repeated, "Dog." Lily said, "Bird." Ben repeated, "Bird." Lily said, "Banana." Ben repeated, "Banana." Lily said, "Lazy." Ben repeated, "Lazy."

Ben felt angry. He thought Lily was cheating. He said, "That's not a word! That's a silly sound! You made it up!" Lily said, "No, it's a word! It's a very long word! You're just lazy and dumb!" Ben said, "No, you're lazy and dumb! And mean!"

They started to argue and shout. They pulled the curtain and tore it. They threw toys and books at each other. They made a big mess.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the woods near their homes. One day, they found a small hut made of sticks and leaves. It looked old and gray, but they thought it was a good place to hide and have fun.

"Let's go inside and see what's there," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful. It might be someone's home," Lily said.

They opened the door and saw a big bed, a table, and some pots and pans. There was also a basket full of apples and bread.

"Wow, look at all this food! Can we have some?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it belongs to someone who will come back soon. We should ask first," Lily said.

But Ben was hungry and curious. He grabbed an apple and took a bite. It was sweet and juicy.

"Mmm, this is good. Try one, Lily," he said.

Lily shook her head. She felt bad for taking something that was not theirs.

"No, thank you. I don't want to. We should leave before we get in trouble," she said.

Ben rolled his eyes. He thought Lily was too scared and boring.

"Fine, be that way. But I'm going to stay here and eat more. You can go if you want," he said.

Lily was sad and angry. She did not like how Ben was acting.

"Ben, please come with me. Don't be greedy and rude. Promise me you will leave the hut with me," she said.

Ben sighed. He did not want to argue with Lily. He liked her as a friend.

"OK, OK. I promise. But let me finish this apple first," he said.

Lily nodded. She waited for Ben to finish his apple. But as soon as he did, he saw another one that looked bigger and redder.

"Wow, look at this one. I want to try it too," he said.

He reached for the apple, but before he could touch it, he heard a loud roar. He turned around and saw a big bear standing at the door. The bear was angry and hungry. It had smelled the food and followed the trail to the hut. It saw Ben and Lily and growled.

"Who are you? What are you doing in my hut? This is my food! You are my food!" the bear said.

Ben and Lily were terrified. They realized they had made a big mistake. They had entered the bear's home and eaten his food without permission. They had broken their promise to each other.

"Help! Help! Run, Lily, run!" Ben shouted.

He dropped the apple and ran to the window. He tried to climb out, but the bear was faster. It grabbed him by the leg and pulled him back. It opened its mouth and bit him hard.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! Let me go! Let me go!" Ben cried.

Lily saw what happened and felt sorry for Ben. She wanted to help him, but she was too scared. She ran to the door and escaped. She ran all the way back to her home and told her parents what had happened. They called the police and the animal control. They hoped they could save Ben from the bear.

The moral of the story is: You should not take what is not yours without asking. You should keep your promises to your friends. You should listen to your conscience and be respectful of others. If you don't, you might face the consequences.

"Look, Leo, look!" Mia said. "The bird is so big and strong. It can soar high and fast. I wish I could soar like that."

"Me too, Mia, me too," Leo said. "Maybe we can find its nest and see its babies. Do you think they are cute?"

They followed the eagle with their eyes until it landed on a tall cliff. They saw a pile of sticks and leaves on the edge. It was the eagle's nest.

"Let's go, Mia, let's go!" Leo said. "We can climb the cliff and peek at the nest. Maybe the eagle will let us touch its babies."

But the eagle saw them. It was not happy. It did not want anyone near its nest. It flew out of the nest and made a loud noise. It was a warning.

"Go away, go away!" the eagle said. "This is my nest and my babies. You are not welcome here. You are too small and weak. You cannot soar like me. You are not brilliant like me."

"Sorry, sorry!" Mia said. "We did not mean to bother you. We just wanted to see your nest and your babies. We think you are brilliant and we admire you."

The fairy shrunk Timmy and he ran through the fence to play in the park. But then, he saw a big dog who wanted to play with him. Timmy was scared because the dog was bigger than him. He asked the fairy to make him big again, but the fairy said she couldn't do it. Timmy was sad and started to cry.

Just then, Timmy's mommy came looking for him and saw him crying. She asked him what was wrong and he told her everything. His mommy hugged him and said that she would take him to another park. Timmy was happy again and thanked the fairy for helping him play in the park, even if it was only for a little while.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily woke up early in the morning. She felt dirty from playing outside the day before, so she decided to take a shower. The water was very cold and rough on her skin, but she knew it would make her clean. 

After the shower, Lily went to the kitchen where her mommy was making breakfast. She said "Thank you mommy" for making pancakes. The pancakes were very yummy and Lily ate them all up. 

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. They played on the swings, went down the slide, and had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Lily said "Thank you" to her friends for playing with her. She was very happy and went to bed with a smile on her face. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing soccer with his friends. His goal was to become the best soccer player in the world. 

One day, Timmy was playing soccer with his friends, but he couldn't score a goal. He became frustrated and sat on the ground. His friend, Johnny, came over and asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?" 

Timmy replied, "I can't score a goal. I want to become the best soccer player in the world, but I can't even score one goal." 

Johnny said, "Don't worry, Timmy. You'll get better with practice. I believe in you." Timmy smiled and got back up to play. He didn't score a goal that day, but he didn't feel frustrated anymore. He knew he had a goal to work towards and he was determined to become the best soccer player in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to climb things, but he found it difficult to climb up high. One day, he saw a ladder leaning against a tall tree. Timmy wanted to climb the ladder to reach the top of the tree, but he was scared. 

He asked his friend, Sally, to help him. Sally said, "I guess we can climb it together." So, they climbed the ladder step by step. It was a bit scary, but they helped each other and finally reached the top of the tree. 

From the top, they could see the whole town and it was beautiful. Timmy was so happy that he conquered his fear and climbed the ladder. He and Sally climbed down the ladder together and went home, feeling proud of themselves.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a loyal dog named Max. Max loved to play and run with Timmy. One day, Timmy and Max went for a walk. Timmy brought his pencil with him to draw pictures. 

As they walked, Timmy saw a big rock. He wanted to climb it, but it was too high. Max barked and wagged his tail, trying to help Timmy. Timmy tried to climb the rock again, but he slipped and fell. Max ran over to Timmy to make sure he was okay. 

Timmy was sad because he couldn't climb the rock. Max licked Timmy's face to cheer him up. Timmy smiled and started to draw a picture of Max and the rock with his pencil. Max sat next to him, being a loyal friend. They had a great day together, even if they couldn't climb the rock. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a job at the store where she helped her mommy sell fruits and vegetables. She loved her job very much and learned how to count money and say hello to customers.

One day, Lily accidentally broke a jar of pickles while trying to put it on the shelf. She felt very sorry and tried to clean up the mess, but it was too late. Her mommy was very angry and told her she couldn't work at the store anymore.

Lily was very sad because she loved her job and wanted to learn more. She went home and cried herself to sleep. The next day, she went to the store to say sorry to her mommy, but she was already replaced by another worker.

From then on, Lily learned to be more careful and never break things again. She missed her job, but she knew she had to be responsible and not make mistakes.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with coins. They had a big jar of coins that their dad gave them. Some coins were shiny and silver, some were dull and brown, and some were bright and copper.

One day, Anna and Ben decided to sort the coins by color. They made three piles on the floor. Anna liked the shiny and silver coins best. She thought they were the most beautiful and valuable. She put them in her pile. Ben liked the bright and copper coins best. He thought they were the most fun and cheerful. He put them in his pile. They both ignored the dull and brown coins. They thought they were the most boring and worthless. They left them in the jar.

"Look at my pile of coins," Anna said. "They are so pretty and sparkly. I have more coins than you."

"No, you don't," Ben said. "Look at my pile of coins. They are so colorful and happy. I have more coins than you."

They started to count their coins. They wanted to see who had more. They counted and counted, but they could not agree. They argued and argued, but they could not settle. They got angry and sad. They did not want to play with each other anymore.

They both sighed. They wished they had more coins. They wished they had more fun. They wished they had more friends.

Then they heard a knock on the door. It was their neighbor, Lily. Lily was a kind and smart girl who liked to read books. She saw the coins on the floor and the jar on the table.

"Hi, Anna and Ben," Lily said. "What are you doing?"

"We are sorting coins by color," Anna said.

"We are counting coins by number," Ben said.

"We are not playing with each other," they both said.

Lily looked at the coins and the jar. She smiled and said, "Can I play with you?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They liked Lily. They wanted to play with her.

Lily picked up the jar and shook it. She said, "Do you know what these coins are? They are not dull and brown. They are clear and gold. They are the most special and rare coins. They are worth more than all the other coins together."

Anna and Ben gasped. They did not know that. They had never looked at the coins closely. They had never seen the clear and gold coins.

Lily opened the jar and poured out the coins. She said, "Let's sort these coins by shape. Some are round, some are square, and some are star-shaped. They are all different and interesting. They are all fun and valuable. They are all coins to share."

Anna and Ben smiled. They liked that idea. They wanted to sort the coins by shape. They wanted to see the different and interesting coins. They wanted to have fun and value the coins. They wanted to share the coins with Lily.

They started to sort the coins by shape. They made three piles on the floor. They did not care about the color or the number of the coins. They cared about the shape and the story of the coins. They talked and laughed and learned. They played and enjoyed and shared. They became happy and friendly and grateful.

They did not sigh anymore. They thanked Lily for playing with them. They thanked their dad for giving them the coins. They thanked each other for being their twins.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge things by their appearance. Look for the beauty and value in everything. Share what you have with others. Be kind and smart and happy.

Ben and Lily were playing hide and seek in the park. Ben was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran behind a big tree and waited for Ben to find her. She giggled as she heard Ben count to ten.

"Ready or not, here I come!" Ben shouted. He looked around the park and saw many places where Lily could hide. He saw a slide, a swing, a bench, and a fountain. He ran to each one and looked behind them, but he did not see Lily.

"Where are you, Lily?" Ben called. "I can't find you!"

Lily heard Ben and smiled. She was very good at hiding. She decided to make a funny noise to tease Ben. She made a loud roar like a lion and waited for Ben's reaction.

Ben heard the roar and jumped. He was scared. He thought there was a real lion in the park. He looked for the source of the roar and saw a shadow behind the tree. He thought it was the lion's shadow. He screamed and ran away.

Lily saw Ben run away and laughed. She realized he was afraid of her roar. She thought it was very funny. She came out from behind the tree and revealed herself.

"Ben, Ben, it's me, Lily!" she shouted. "It was not a lion, it was me! I was hiding behind the tree and I made a roar to trick you!"

Ben stopped running and turned around. He saw Lily and felt silly. He realized he had been fooled by her. He felt stupid.

"Lily, that was not nice!" he said. "You scared me! You made me think there was a lion in the park!"

Lily ran to Ben and hugged him. She was sorry for scaring him. She did not mean to make him feel stupid.

"I'm sorry, Ben, I was just playing," she said. "You are not stupid, you are smart. You are my best friend. Do you want to play again?"

Ben hugged Lily back. He was not angry anymore. He forgave her. He liked playing with her. He was her best friend too.

"Okay, Lily, I forgive you," he said. "Let's play again. But this time, you are the seeker and I am the hider. And no more roars, okay?"

"Okay, Ben, no more roars," Lily said. "But you better hide well, because I will find you!"

They smiled and ran to a new spot. They started a new game of hide and seek. They had fun in the park. They were happy.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. Lily has a big pile of blue blocks. Ben has a big pile of red blocks.

"Look at my tower!" Lily says. "It is very tall and strong. I add more blocks to make it taller."

"Wow, that is a good tower!" Ben says. "But I like my house better. It has a door and a window and a roof. I add more blocks to make it bigger."

They both add more and more blocks to their piles. They are having fun.

Then, they see a shiny yellow block on the floor. It is the only yellow block in the room. It is very pretty and bright.

"Ooh, I want that block!" Lily says. "It is perfect for my tower. It will make it shine."

"No, I want that block!" Ben says. "It is perfect for my house. It will make it cozy."

They both run to the block. They both try to grab it. They both pull and tug and shout.

"Let go, it is mine!" Lily says.

"No, let go, it is mine!" Ben says.

They are not having fun anymore. They are angry and sad.

Then, they hear a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing?" It is Sam, their friend. He is holding a basket of blocks. He has green blocks and purple blocks and orange blocks. He has many blocks.

"We are playing with blocks," Lily says.

"We are fighting over a block," Ben says.

Sam looks at them. He looks at the yellow block. He looks at his basket.

"I have an idea," he says. "Why don't you share the yellow block? You can both use it for your tower and your house. And you can also use some of my blocks. They are very nice and colorful. You can add them to your piles. Then, you can have more fun."

Lily and Ben think about it. They look at each other. They look at the yellow block. They look at Sam's basket.

"OK, that sounds good," Lily says.

"Yes, that sounds good," Ben says.

They let go of the yellow block. They say sorry to each other. They smile and hug.

"Thank you, Sam," they say.

"You're welcome," Sam says. "Let's play together."

They take some blocks from Sam's basket. They add them to their piles. They make their tower and their house more beautiful and fun. They use the yellow block as a star and a sun. They are happy and proud.

They have a good time. They are friends.

"Please, Lily, wear your skirt," her mom said. "It is very pretty and matches your coat. You can wear your leggings under it, so you will not be cold."

Lily shook her head. She did not like leggings. They were too tight and itchy. She wanted to wear her jeans. They were cozy and soft.

Her mom saw that Lily was unhappy. She did not want to make her wear something she did not like. She wanted to encourage her to try new things and have fun.

"How about this, Lily?" her mom said. "You can wear your jeans today, but tomorrow you can wear your skirt and we will go to the park. There is a big slide there that you love. Maybe you can show your skirt to your friends and they will like it too."

Lily thought about it. She liked the park and the slide. She liked her friends. Maybe they would think her skirt was pretty. Maybe she would feel pretty too.

"Okay, mom," she said. "I will wear my skirt tomorrow. But today I want to wear my jeans."

Her mom smiled and hugged her. "That sounds good, Lily. You are a very smart and brave girl. I love you."

Lily smiled back and said, "I love you too, mom." She put on her jeans and ran outside to play. She felt warm and happy.

Sara loved her dog, Spot. Spot was a big dog with black and white fur. He liked to run, play and bark. Sara gave him a new collar for his birthday. The collar was red and shiny. It had a bell that made a sound when Spot moved.

"Look, Spot, your new collar is so beautiful!" Sara said. "Do you like it?" Spot wagged his tail and licked Sara's face. He liked his new collar very much.

One day, Sara and Spot went to the park. They saw many other dogs and people. Spot wanted to say hello to everyone. He ran and jumped and barked. His bell rang loud and clear. Sara laughed and followed him.

But not everyone liked Spot's bell. A mean boy came up to Sara and Spot. He had a stick in his hand. He said, "Your dog is too noisy. His bell is annoying. I don't like it."

Sara felt scared and angry. She said, "Don't be rude. Spot is a good dog. His collar is a gift. I love it."

The mean boy did not listen. He swung his stick at Spot. He tried to hit his collar and break it. Spot dodged the stick and growled. He did not like the mean boy.

Sara shouted, "Stop it! Leave us alone!" She grabbed Spot's collar and pulled him away. She ran to find her mom. She told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and Spot. She said, "I'm sorry, Sara. That boy was very mean. He should not have tried to hurt you or Spot. You did the right thing to run away. You are brave and kind. You and Spot are a great team."

Sara smiled and hugged her mom and Spot. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you and Spot. Spot loves his collar and I love him. His bell is not annoying. It is music to my ears."

The moral value of the story is: Respect others and their belongings. Don't be mean or violent. Love and protect your friends.

"See, he likes you," Lily says.

"Hello, dog," Tom says.

The dog barks. He is happy. He likes Tom and Lily.

Tom and Sue agree. They go with their moms. Tom sees the snakes. He likes them. He sees a big snake. It is green and yellow. It has a cut on its tail. Tom feels sorry for the snake. He says, "Mom, look, that snake has a cut. It must be weak and sad. Can we help it?"

His mom says, "No, Tom, we can't help it. The zookeepers will help it. They know how to take care of snakes. We can only look and not touch. Snakes are wild animals. They can be dangerous. Come, let's go see the other snakes."

Tom nods. He says, "Okay, mom. But I hope the snake gets better soon. It is a nice snake."

Her mom says, "No, Sue, you can't pet it. The elephants are behind a fence. We can only look and not touch. Elephants are wild animals. They can be dangerous. Come, let's go see the other elephants."

Sue nods. She says, "Okay, mom. But I wish I could pet it. It is a nice elephant."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dad. They saw some people hitting balls with sticks on a big green field. They wanted to try it too.

"Dad, can we play golf?" Lily asked.

"Sorry, sweetie, golf is not for kids. It is too hard and dangerous. You might get hurt or break something," dad said.

"But dad, it looks so fun!" Ben said.

"Maybe when you are older, you can learn golf. But for now, let's go to the swings and slides, okay?" dad said.

Lily and Ben nodded, but they were still curious about golf. They followed dad to the playground, but they kept looking at the golf field. They saw a big pile of balls and sticks near a fence. They had an idea.

"Hey, Lily, let's sneak over there and get some balls and sticks. We can play golf behind the fence, where dad can't see us," Ben whispered.

"Okay, let's go. But we have to be quick and quiet," Lily whispered back.

They waited until dad was busy talking to another parent. Then they ran to the pile of balls and sticks. They each grabbed one stick and one ball. They climbed over the fence and found a spot behind some trees. They tried to hit the ball with the stick, but it was harder than it looked. The ball went too high, too low, or not at all. They kept trying, but they also made a lot of noise.

"Wow, this is fun!" Ben said.

"Yeah, but I feel guilty. We are not supposed to do this. What if dad finds out?" Lily said.

"Relax, he won't find out. We are too smart for him," Ben said.

But he was wrong. Dad heard the noise and saw the fence moving. He walked over and saw Lily and Ben playing golf with the balls and sticks. He was not happy.

"Lily! Ben! What are you doing? You know you are not allowed to play golf! You could have hurt yourself or someone else! And you took the balls and sticks without asking! That is very naughty and rude!" dad said.

Lily and Ben dropped the balls and sticks. They looked at dad with scared and sorry faces. They knew they were in trouble.

"Dad, we are sorry. We just wanted to try golf. It looked so fun. We didn't mean to be naughty and rude," Lily said.

"Dad, we are sorry. We won't do it again. We promise. Please don't be mad at us," Ben said.

Dad sighed. He was angry, but he also loved his kids. He knew they were curious and adventurous. He decided to give them a chance to learn from their mistake.

"Okay, I forgive you. But you have to apologize to the golf people and return the balls and sticks. And you have to promise me that you will never play golf without my permission and supervision. Do you understand?" dad said.

"Yes, dad, we understand. We are sorry. We love you," Lily and Ben said.

They hugged dad and said sorry to the golf people. They returned the balls and sticks. They learned their lesson. They decided to play on the swings and slides instead. They had fun, but they also respected the rules. They were happy and proud. Dad was happy and proud too.

One day, she saw a big bird in the sky. She thought it would be fun to shoot at it with her bow and arrow. She did not listen to the bird, who cried out, "Please, do not hurt me! I have a nest and babies to feed!" She aimed and fired, and hit the bird in the wing.

The bird fell to the ground, and Lily ran to see what she had done. She saw the bird was bleeding and miserable. She felt sorry and scared. She did not know what to do. She cried, "I am sorry, bird! I did not mean to hurt you!"

The bird looked at her with sad eyes, and said, "Why did you shoot me? I did not do anything to you. You should listen to your mom and dad, and to the animals, who have feelings too. You should be kind and gentle, not cruel and mean."

Lily realized she had been very bad. She said, "You are right, bird. I was very bad. I will listen to my mom and dad, and to the animals, from now on. I will be kind and gentle, not cruel and mean. Can you forgive me?"

The bird said, "I forgive you, Lily. But you have to help me. I need to go back to my nest and babies. Can you take me there?"

Lily nodded, and carefully picked up the bird. She followed the bird's directions, and took him to his nest in a tall tree. There, she saw the bird's babies, who were hungry and worried. She helped the bird feed them, and bandage his wing. She said, "I am sorry, bird's babies. I hurt your dad. I will not do it again."

The bird's babies said, "Thank you, Lily. You helped our dad. You are not bad. You are good."

Lily smiled, and felt happy. She had learned a lesson. She said, "Goodbye, bird and bird's babies. I hope you get well soon. I will come back and visit you, but I will not shoot at you. I will bring you seeds and berries."

The bird said, "Goodbye, Lily. Thank you for helping me and my babies. You are a brave and good girl. I hope you have fun with your bow and arrow, but use them wisely and kindly."

Lily waved, and ran back to her mom and dad. She told them what had happened, and said she was sorry. They hugged her, and said they were proud of her. They said, "You made a mistake, but you fixed it. You learned to listen, and to be kind and gentle. That is what makes you a brave and good girl."

Lily felt happy and loved. She played with her bow and arrow, but she used them wisely and kindly. She listened to her mom and dad, and to the animals. She had many friends in the forest, and they all liked her. She was a brave and good girl.

When she got home, her mom was very surprised to see the potato. "What a lucky find!" she said. Lily helped her mom cook the potato for dinner and it was delicious. From that day on, Lily always kept her eyes open for lucky potatoes on her walks.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a regular day at school, but when he got home, he saw his little sister, Lily, had wrapped his favorite toy car in a blanket. Timmy got upset and slapped the blanket off the toy car.

Lily started crying and ran to their mom. Their mom asked Timmy why he slapped the blanket off the toy car. Timmy explained that it was his favorite toy car and he didn't like it being wrapped up.

Their mom helped them work out a solution. She suggested they take turns playing with the toy car and that Lily could wrap it up when it was her turn. Timmy agreed and apologized for slapping the blanket off the toy car. In the end, they were both happy and played together nicely.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl called Sue. Sue was 3 years old and she liked Wednesday. Every Wednesday, she would go to the stream to bathe.

One Wednesday, Sue went to the stream as usual and she wanted to bathe. She looked around but there were no buckets or cups to carry the water. Sue started to cry as she didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a kind voice said, "Don't cry, little Sue." Sue looked up and saw a fairy. The fairy said, "I can help you bathe." Sue smiled and nodded in agreement.

The fairy waved her wand and filled the stream with warm and bubbly water. Sue got in and it felt so wonderful. She had a great time splashing about in the warm water.

The fairy said goodbye and Sue thanked her for the wonderful bath. After she finished, Sue went home happy and clean. She looked forward to the next Wednesday so she could bathe in the stream again.

"I have been here since before the trees began to rot. I have seen many animals come and go".

Daddy came home from work and saw them playing. He smiled and said, "What are you doing, my little ones?"

"We are sorting by sound, Daddy," Lily said. "Look, we have a vroom pile, a mama pile, a bang pile, and a beep pile."

"That's very clever, Lily," Daddy said. "And what about you, Max? What pile do you like best?"

Max pointed to the robot and said, "I like the beep pile, Daddy. The robot is powerful. It can do many things."

Daddy picked up the robot and said, "You are right, Max. The robot is powerful. But do you know who is more powerful than the robot?"

Max shook his head and said, "Who, Daddy?"

Daddy hugged him and said, "You are, Max. And so is Lily. And so am I. We are powerful because we have love. Love is the most powerful thing in the world."

Lily and Max smiled and hugged Daddy back. They felt happy and warm. They agreed that love was the most powerful thing in the world. And they loved to sort their toys.

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the ambulance. He opened the door and climbed inside. He saw many things. He saw a bed, a bag, a mask, a needle. He wanted to keep them.

"Tom, come out!" Lily shouted. "You are being bad. The ambulance people will be angry."

But Tom did not listen. He played with the things. He put the mask on his face. He pressed the bag. He poked the needle. He made a wild mess.

Then the ambulance people came back. They saw Tom inside. They were very angry. They grabbed Tom and pulled him out. They yelled at him. They said he was naughty. They said he broke their things. They said he could have hurt himself or someone else.

Tom was scared. He cried. He wanted Lily. He wanted his mom. He wanted to go home.

But the ambulance people did not let him go. They said he had to go with them. They said he had to pay for what he did. They said he had to learn a lesson.

They put Tom in the back of the ambulance. They closed the door. They drove away.

Lily was sad. She watched the ambulance leave. She did not know where Tom was going. She did not know if she would see him again. She wished he had listened to her. She wished he had stayed away.

He found a shady tree and lay down under it. He wanted to rest his legs and his mouth. He closed his eyes and started to sleep. He dreamed of juicy meat and happy lions.

But he did not hear a sneaky hyena coming near him. The hyena smelled the lion and saw his big paws and teeth. He was scared, but he was also hungry. He wanted to steal some of the lion's meat.

He crept closer and closer to the lion, hoping he would not wake up. He reached the lion's tail and bit it hard. He thought he could pull it and run away with it.

But the lion woke up with a roar. He was angry and wild. He jumped up and chased the hyena away. He bit his back and made him yelp. He taught him a lesson.

The hyena ran and ran, never looking back. He learned not to mess with the lion and his meat. The lion went back to his tree and rested again. He hoped to find some meat tomorrow. He was still hungry, but he was also proud.

Tom and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks. The ducks were swimming and quacking. Tom and Lily liked the ducks. They wanted to feed them some bread.

Mom gave them some bread and said, "Be nice to the ducks. Don't throw the bread too hard. Don't chase them or scare them. They are living things, like us. They have feelings, too."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "OK, Mom." They broke the bread into small pieces and threw them gently to the ducks. The ducks came closer and ate the bread. They seemed happy and friendly.

Tom saw a duck that was smaller and fluffier than the others. It had yellow feathers and a pink beak. Tom thought it was very cute. He wanted to pick it up and hug it. He said to Lily, "Look at that duck. It's so cute. I want to pick it up."

Lily said, "No, Tom. Don't do that. Mom said be nice to the ducks. The duck might not like it. It might be scared or hurt. It might bite you or flap its wings. It might miss its mom or dad. Let it be with its friends."

Tom said, "But I just want to hold it for a little bit. It won't mind. It will like me." He reached out his hand to grab the duck.

The duck saw Tom's hand and got scared. It quacked loudly and tried to swim away. But Tom was faster. He picked up the duck and lifted it in the air.

The duck was very unhappy. It felt trapped and scared. It bit Tom's finger and flapped its wings. It quacked louder and louder.

Tom felt a sharp pain in his finger. He dropped the duck and cried. He said, "Ow, ow, ow! The duck bit me! It hurt me!"

Mom heard Tom's cry and ran to him. She saw his finger bleeding and the duck swimming away. She said, "Oh, Tom. What did you do? Why did you pick up the duck? Didn't I tell you to be nice to the ducks?"

Tom said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted to hug the duck. It was so cute. I didn't mean to make it mad."

Mom said, "I know, Tom. But you have to respect the ducks. They are not toys. They are living things, like us. They have feelings, too. They don't like to be picked up by strangers. They like to be free and safe. You have to be gentle and kind to them. That's how you show them you care."

Tom said, "I understand, Mom. I'm sorry. I won't pick up the ducks again. I will be nice to them. I will feed them and watch them and talk to them. But I won't touch them."

Mom said, "That's good, Tom. I'm proud of you. Now let me clean your finger and put a band-aid on it. It will heal soon. And maybe the duck will forgive you, too."

Tom said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you. And I love the ducks, too."

Mom said, "I love you, too, Tom. And I'm sure the ducks love you, too. As long as you are nice to them."

Lily's mommy told her that the doll was very famous and many people wanted it. She said they would have to save up some money to buy it. So, Lily and her mommy started to save their money every week. They would put their money in a jar and store it in a safe place.

After a few weeks, they had enough money to buy the luxury doll. Lily was so happy and she played with her new doll every day. She knew it was a special toy because it was famous and she had to save up for it. From then on, Lily learned the importance of saving money and how it can help you get the things you really want.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty princess named Lily. She lived in a big castle with her parents, the king and queen. One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest and met a talking frog.

"Hello, pretty princess!" said the frog.

"Hi, Mr. Frog! Why do you talk?" asked Lily.

"I don't know. Maybe it's because I ate some magic oil," replied the frog.

"Wow! Can I have some magic oil too?" asked Lily.

"I'm afraid not, pretty princess. The oil only works for frogs. But maybe I can help you with something else. What do you need?" said the frog.

"Well, I wish I could shrink myself and explore the forest even more!" said Lily.

"Okay, I can help with that. Just close your eyes and say 'shrink' three times," said the frog.

Lily did as she was told and suddenly she became very small. She explored the forest and had lots of fun. When she was ready to go back to her normal size, she said 'grow' three times and she became big again.

"Thank you, Mr. Frog! That was so much fun!" said Lily.

"You're welcome, pretty princess. Come visit me anytime you want to shrink again!" said the frog.

And from that day on, Lily visited the talking frog in the forest whenever she wanted to have a magical adventure.

"Okay, Mom, we are coming," Tom says. He puts on his blue shoes and his red coat. He grabs his ball and his truck.

"I want to go too," Lily says. She puts on her pink shoes and her yellow coat. She takes her doll and her purse.

Tom and Lily run to the car. They see Dad smiling. He helps them buckle their seat belts.

"Are you ready for some fun?" Dad asks.

"Yes, yes, yes!" Tom and Lily say.

They drive to the park. They see other kids playing. They see the big slide, the swing, and the sandbox.

"Can we go to the slide first?" Tom asks.

"Can we go to the swing first?" Lily asks.

Dad laughs. He says, "How about we take turns? Tom, you can go to the slide first. Lily, you can go to the swing first. Then you can switch. How does that sound?"

Tom and Lily nod. They say, "Okay, Dad, that sounds fair."

They jump out of the car. They run to the slide and the swing. They have fun. They are patient. They share. They laugh. They hug. They thank Dad for taking them to the park. They are happy.

Jill liked to play in the garden. She liked to dig in the dirt and find insects. She liked to look at their legs and wings and colors. She liked to make them homes in jars and cups. She liked to feed them leaves and water.

One day, she found a big insect in the garden. It was brown and hairy and had many legs. It looked like a worm, but bigger and stronger. Jill was happy. She wanted to keep it as a pet. She put it in a big jar and gave it some leaves and water. She named it Fuzzy.

Jill took Fuzzy to her room and put him on her shelf. She looked at him every day and said hello. She thought he was happy too. But Fuzzy was not happy. He did not like the jar. He did not like the leaves and water. He wanted to be in the dirt. He wanted to eat other things. He was troubled.

Fuzzy started to change. He became thinner and weaker. His legs and hairs fell off. His color faded. He smelled bad. He was rotting. Jill did not notice. She was busy with other things. She forgot to look at him. She forgot to say hello.

One day, Jill remembered Fuzzy. She ran to her room and looked at the jar. She saw something that made her scream. Fuzzy was gone. In his place, there was a pile of dust and bones. And on top of the pile, there was a new insect. It was black and shiny and had wings. It looked like a beetle, but bigger and scarier. It was Fuzzy's baby. It had eaten Fuzzy. It was hungry. It looked at Jill and hissed.

Tom has a loose tooth. He can wiggle it with his tongue. He is not scared. He knows that when his tooth falls out, a new one will grow. He also knows that the tooth fairy will bring him a coin if he puts his tooth under his pillow.

One day, Tom is eating an apple. He bites hard and feels a pop. He spits out a piece of apple and sees his tooth on it. He is happy. He runs to show his mom. She smiles and hugs him. She says he is a big boy and his tooth is fine. She gives him a small box to keep his tooth safe.

That night, Tom puts his tooth in the box and the box under his pillow. He falls asleep fast. He dreams of the tooth fairy. He wonders what she looks like and what she will bring him. He hopes it is a shiny coin.

In the morning, Tom wakes up and feels under his pillow. He finds the box and opens it. He sees a coin inside. He is excited. He jumps out of bed and runs to show his mom. She is proud of him. She says the tooth fairy brought him a coin for his tooth. She says he can buy something he likes with it.

Tom is happy. He thanks the tooth fairy in his mind. He thinks losing a tooth is fine. He wonders when his next tooth will fall out. He hopes it will be soon. He wants to see the tooth fairy again.

But today, Ben felt a tickle in his nose. He tried to hold it in, but he could not. He sneezed very loud, and everyone in the barber shop looked at him. "Bless you," said the barber. "Are you okay, Ben?"

Ben nodded, but he sneezed again. And again. And again. He sneezed so much that his dad had to take him outside. The barber followed them with a worried face. "I'm sorry, Ben," he said. "You can't get your hair cut today. You might have a cold. You need to go home and rest."

Ben was sad. He wanted to get his hair cut and get his sticker and his lollipop. He looked at the barber shop, where he saw a bright sign that said "Come back soon". He hoped he would feel better soon, and come back to the barber. He smiled at the barber and said, "Thank you. I will come back soon. And I will not sneeze."

Anna and Ben are friends. They live in a big country with many mountains and snow. They like to play outside and make snowmen and snowballs. Sometimes they go to the lake and slide on the icy water.

One day, they find a broken sled near the lake. It has a hole in the bottom and a loose rope. Anna and Ben want to ride the sled, but they know it is not safe.

"Can we repair the sled?" Anna asks Ben.

"Maybe we can," Ben says. "We need some wood and glue and a new rope."

They look around and see a small hut. They knock on the door and a kind man opens it. He has a beard and a hat and a big smile.

"Hello, children. What can I do for you?" he says.

"Please, sir, can you help us repair this sled?" Anna says. "We want to ride it on the lake."

The man looks at the sled and nods. "Sure, I can help you. I have some tools and materials in my hut. Come in and let's fix it together."

Anna and Ben follow the man into the hut. They see many things inside: a stove, a table, a bed, a shelf, and a box. The man takes out some wood and glue and a new rope from the box. He shows Anna and Ben how to patch the hole, tighten the rope, and smooth the edges.

"There, the sled is ready. You can ride it now, but be careful. The lake is very icy and slippery," he says.

"Thank you, sir. You are very nice," Anna and Ben say.

They take the sled and go outside. They run to the lake and put the sled on the ice. They take turns riding it and having fun. They laugh and shout and wave to the man in the hut. They are happy. They have repaired the sled and made a new friend.

One day, when Lily and her mom were at the zoo, they saw a big cage with a sign that said "New Parrot". Lily ran to the cage and looked inside. She saw a parrot that was very different from the other parrots. It was gray and had no feathers on its head. It looked sad and scared.

Lily felt sorry for the new parrot. She asked her mom, "Why is the parrot like that? Why does it have no feathers?"

Her mom said, "The parrot was hurt by some bad people. They took it from its home and did not take care of it. They made it do tricks and pulled its feathers. The zoo people rescued the parrot and brought it here. They are trying to help it, but it is very sick and weak."

Lily wanted to help the parrot too. She said, "Can I talk to the parrot? Maybe it will feel better if it has a friend."

Her mom said, "You can try, but be careful. The parrot might be scared of you and bite you. It does not trust anyone yet."

Lily nodded and slowly approached the cage. She said softly, "Hello, parrot. My name is Lily. I like you. You are very pretty. Do you want to talk to me?"

The parrot looked at Lily with its dark eyes. It did not say anything. It just shivered and hid in a corner.

Lily did not give up. She came back to the cage every day and talked to the parrot. She told it stories and jokes and sang songs. She brought it seeds and fruits and water. She was gentle and kind.

Gradually, the parrot started to listen to Lily. It moved closer to the cage bars and tilted its head. It made some noises and copied some of Lily's words. It ate some of the food and drank some of the water. It looked less sad and scared.

One day, Lily was very happy. The parrot said to her, "Hello, Lily. I like you. You are my friend."

Lily smiled and said, "Hello, parrot. I like you too. You are my friend. What is your name?"

The parrot said, "My name is Coco. Thank you for helping me. You are very nice."

Lily and Coco hugged each other through the cage bars. They were both very happy. They had learned to trust each other.

"Oh no, our boats!" Tom and Sam cried. They ran to the water and tried to get their boats back. But the wind was too strong and the water was too deep. They could not reach their boats.

When the corner was gone, he carefully reached in and grabbed the cheese. He was so happy! He ate the cheese and it was delicious. He stayed careful and never forgot how dangerous sharp corners can be.

But then Eddie noticed something strange. Marvin was not only still unamused, he seemed to actually be laughing! Eddie was surprised. It turned out that Marvin loved it when Eddie joked around. From that day onwards, the two friends joked around together every day.

Baby frowned. She sighed. "Do we have to leave?" she asked.

Mama nodded. "Yes, we have to go home and bathe," she said. 

Baby was confused. Bathe? What was that?

Mama smiled. "You'll see when we get home," she said in a cheerful voice.
