Sandy was excited, so she hopped closer and hopped around it in circles.

She could see a warm glow emanating from the lamp, and as she jumped around, it began to sway back and forth. Suddenly, a tiny voice came from inside the lamp: "Can I help you?" Sandy stopped still and stared in amazement. A fairy was inside the lamp!

The fairy was happy to see Sandy, so she waved her wand and said, "I've been stuck here for a long time, so let's have some fun! Let's see who can bounce the highest!"

Sandy was delighted, and with a big hop, she got ready to bounce. The fairy and Sandy took turns, each one trying to jump higher than the other. Sandy was so light, she kept jumping higher and higher, until she was bouncing almost as high as the tree branches! Sandy laughed as she jumped, while the lamp swayed and the fairy twinkled with joy. In the end, it was a fun day of bouncing for Sandy and the fairy!

"I'm crying because I'm so small and all the other sunflowers are so big and beautiful," replied the sunflower.

"Don't cry, little sunflower," said Lily. "You may be small, but you are still incredible and special just like the others."

The little sunflower smiled and stopped crying. From that day on, Lily made sure to visit the little sunflower every day and give it extra love and attention.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and twirl around in her room. One day, she saw a gray cat outside her window. 

"Hello, little kitty," said Lily. "Do you want to dance with me?" 

The cat meowed and Lily took that as a yes. They danced and twirled together for hours. Suddenly, the cat became a dancer! 

"You're a great dancer, kitty," said Lily. 

The cat meowed happily and they continued to dance together. When it was time for Lily to go to bed, she said goodbye to the gray dancer and went to sleep with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved aeroplanes, and he always wanted to go on one. One day, his mommy said, "Timmy, we're going on an aeroplane tomorrow to visit your grandma. But you have to go to bed early tonight, or you'll be too sleepy in the morning."

Timmy didn't want to go to bed early, but he really wanted to go on the aeroplane. So he said, "Mommy, please can I stay up a little bit longer? I promise I won't be too sleepy in the morning."

Mommy thought about it for a moment and said, "Okay, but only for a little bit. Then it's off to bed for you, young man."

Timmy was so happy that he got to stay up a little bit longer. He played with his toys and watched some TV. But eventually, he started to feel very sleepy. So he went to bed, dreaming about flying on an aeroplane to see his grandma.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike. He always wore his helmet to keep him safe. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came to play. Billy didn't have a helmet, so Timmy gave him his own helmet to wear. Timmy was being generous.

Tom liked to use his red bike to go to the park. He liked to see the trees, the flowers and the animals. He liked to feed the squirrels with nuts and seeds. He always brought a big bag of food for them.

One day, he saw a new squirrel in the park. It was small and gray, with a long bushy tail. It looked hungry and scared. Tom wanted to help it. He took some nuts from his bag and threw them to the new squirrel. But the other squirrels were not happy. They ran to the nuts and chased the new squirrel away. They were greedy and mean.

Tom felt sorry for the new squirrel. He decided to do something nice for it. He got off his bike and walked to a big tree. He saw the new squirrel hiding in a hole. He smiled and said, "Hello, little squirrel. Don't be afraid. I have a gift for you." He took out his red bike and put it near the hole. He said, "This is my bike. I like to use it to go to the park. But you can use it too. You can ride it and have fun. It is yours now. I am generous. I like to share."

The new squirrel was surprised and curious. It came out of the hole and sniffed the bike. It touched the wheels, the pedals and the handlebars. It climbed on the seat and held the grips. It felt happy and grateful. It said, "Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. You are generous. You are my friend." It gave Tom a big hug and a nut.

Tom and the new squirrel became friends. They played together in the park. They used the bike to explore and have adventures. They shared the food and the fun. They were happy and generous. The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Anna wants to go on the slide, but Ben is scared.

"Come on, Ben, it is fun!" Anna says. "You can manage it. I will go first and show you."

Anna runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. She sits on the slide and slides down. She laughs and shouts, "Whee!"

Ben watches Anna. He wants to try, but he is still scared. He walks to the slide and holds the ladder. He takes a deep breath and climbs up. He looks down and feels dizzy.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Anna asks. She is at the bottom of the slide. She smiles and waves at him.

"I am okay, Anna," Ben says. He tries to be brave. He sits on the slide and slides down. But he slides too fast and falls off. He lands on the grass and hurts his knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cries. He holds his knee and tears roll down his face.

Anna runs to Ben. She hugs him and says, "I am sorry, Ben. Are you hurt?"

Ben nods and sniffles. He shows Anna his knee. It is red and bleeding.

Anna says, "Don't worry, Ben. I have a band-aid in my backpack. I will put it on your knee. It will make you feel better."

Anna takes out a band-aid and sticks it on Ben's knee. She kisses his cheek and says, "There, all done. Does it feel better?"

Ben smiles and says, "Yes, thank you, Anna. You are a good friend."

Anna says, "You are welcome, Ben. You are a good friend, too. You tried the slide. You are brave."

Ben says, "Thank you, Anna. But I don't like the slide. It is too high and too fast. I like the swings better. They are more comfortable."

Anna says, "That's okay, Ben. We can play on the swings. They are fun, too. Come on, let's go."

Anna and Ben hold hands and walk to the swings. They swing and laugh and have a good time. They forget about the trip and the slide. They are happy.

Tim and Liz nod. They want to try the new shampoo. Mom puts some shampoo on their heads. She rubs it gently. The shampoo makes many bubbles. The bubbles are white and fluffy. They look like snow.

"Wow, look at the bubbles!" Tim says. He blows on the bubbles. They fly in the air. He tries to catch them with his hands.

"Me too, me too!" Liz says. She also blows on the bubbles. They fly in the air. She tries to catch them with her mouth.

Mom smiles. She thinks they are funny. She says, "You two are so silly. You are not supposed to eat the bubbles. They are not food. They are soap. They taste bad."

Tim and Liz spit out the bubbles. They make a face. They say, "Yuck, yuck, yuck!"

Mom rinses their hair with water. She says, "Now your hair is clean and nice. Let me dry it with a towel."

Tim and Liz wrap themselves in the towel. They hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. And we love the new shampoo. It is fun to play with the bubbles."

She looked out the window. She saw her friends running and laughing in the park. They had balls and bikes and kites. They looked so happy. Lily felt sad. She wished she could join them.

She put down her pencil. She got up from her chair. She ran to the door. She grabbed her coat. She opened the door.

"Lily, where are you going?" Mom called.

"I'm going out, Mom. I'm done with my homework. Bye!" Lily said.

She ran out the door. She did not hear Mom say, "Lily, you are not done. You have to write F, G, and H. Come back here!"

Lily did not come back. She ran to the park. She played with her friends. She had fun. She forgot about her homework. She did not know that Mom was angry. She did not know that she would have to study more later. She did not know that she made a mistake.

She knocked on his door and saw him sitting on the couch. He looked bored and unhappy.

"Hi, Ben," Lily said, holding out the jewel. "I'm sorry I was mean to you. I want to share the jewel with you. You can have it if you want."

Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He was glad she came and said sorry. He didn't care about the jewel anymore. He just wanted to play with her.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, but they did not put them away when they were done. They were careless and left them on the floor, on the couch, and on the table.

"Let's go outside and play with the ball," Tom said.

"OK, but first we have to finish our snack," Lily said.

They went to the kitchen and ate some cookies and milk. They did not finish their snack, either. They left some crumbs and a half-empty glass on the counter.

They ran outside and played with the ball. They had fun, but they did not hear their mom calling them.

"Tom! Lily! Come inside, it's getting dark!" Mom said.

They did not listen. They kept playing with the ball.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a big, scary monster. It had fur, horns, teeth, and claws. It was angry and hungry. It saw the children and their ball.

"Roar! I am the monster of the night! I come to eat careless children who do not finish their toys, their snacks, and their chores! Give me your ball, or I will eat you!" the monster said.

Lily and Tom were very afraid. They dropped the ball and ran to the house. They knocked on the door and cried for their mom.

"Mom! Mom! Help us! There is a monster outside!" they said.

Mom opened the door and let them in. She hugged them and calmed them down.

"What monster? What are you talking about?" Mom said.

Lily and Tom told her about the monster of the night. Mom looked outside and saw the ball. She smiled and said:

"That is not a monster, that is Mr. Brown, our neighbor. He likes to dress up and scare children who do not listen to their parents. He is not really mean, he is just trying to teach you a lesson. You should be more careful and finish your toys, your snacks, and your chores. Then, you will not have to worry about monsters or Mr. Brown."

Lily and Tom felt ashamed and sorry. They said:

"We are sorry, Mom. We were careless and did not finish our things. We will be more careful and finish our things from now on. We do not want to see the monster of the night again."

Mom smiled and said:

"That's good, my loves. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's go and finish your things together. And maybe, we can say sorry to Mr. Brown and get your ball back."

Lily and Tom nodded and said:

"OK, Mom. Thank you for saving us from the monster of the night."

They went and finished their things. They also said sorry to Mr. Brown and got their ball back. They learned to be more careful and finish their things. They never saw the monster of the night again.

Sam and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Sam!" Lily said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a castle or a dragon!"

Sam was not sure. He looked at the sky. It was getting dark and cloudy. He felt a cold wind. He was scared.

"I don't know, Lily," he said. "It looks like a storm is coming. Maybe we should go back to our mom and dad. They are waiting for us in the car."

Lily did not listen. She was too excited. She ran to the hill and started to climb. She removed her coat and hat and left them on the ground. She did not want to be hot or slow.

"Come on, Sam!" she shouted. "Don't be a baby! It's fun!"

Sam did not want to be a baby. He wanted to be brave. He followed Lily to the hill. He removed his coat and hat too. He did not want to lose her.

They climbed and climbed. They reached the top of the hill. They looked at the other side. They saw a big road with a lot of cars. They saw a sign that said "West". They did not see any treasure or castle or dragon.

"Is this it?" Sam asked. "This is boring. Let's go back."

Lily agreed. She was disappointed. She turned around. She saw the storm. It was very close. It was very loud. It had lightning and thunder. She was scared.

"Sam, we have to hurry!" she said. "The storm is here!"

They ran down the hill. They looked for their coats and hats. They could not find them. The wind had blown them away. They were cold and wet.

They reached the park. They looked for their mom and dad. They could not find them. The car was gone. They were alone.

They cried. They did not know what to do. They did not know where to go. They did not know how to get home.

The end.

Anna and Ben were upset. They wanted to see the mountain so much. They went to the yard and sat on the grass. They looked at the mountain and frowned.

"Why can't we go to the mountain, Anna?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe Mom is scared of the mountain. Maybe there are bad things on the mountain. Maybe the mountain is not for us," Anna said.

Tom was a bald man who liked to order pizza. He always called the same pizza place and asked for cheese and ham. He knew the pizza man's voice very well.

One day, Tom wanted to order pizza again. He picked up the phone and dialed the number. But he heard a different voice. It was a woman's voice. She said, "Hello, this is Lisa. How can I help you?"

Tom was surprised. He said, "Who are you? Where is the pizza man?"

Lisa said, "I'm sorry, the pizza man is sick today. I'm his sister. I'm helping him with the orders. What would you like?"

Tom said, "I want cheese and ham pizza. Please hurry. I'm very hungry."

Lisa said, "Okay, no problem. I'll make your pizza and bring it to you soon. What is your address?"

Tom told her his address and hung up the phone. He wondered if Lisa would make his pizza as good as the pizza man.

After a while, there was a knock on the door. Tom opened it and saw Lisa. She had a big smile and a pizza box. She also had something else. It was a hat. A hat with ears.

She said, "Hi, Tom. I'm Lisa. Here is your cheese and ham pizza. I hope you like it. And I have a gift for you. It's a hat. A hat with ears. I made it myself. I thought you might like it. It will keep your head warm and make you look funny."

Tom was confused. He said, "A hat with ears? Why do I need a hat with ears? I already have ears."

Lisa said, "But your ears are small and hidden. This hat has big and fluffy ears. Like a bunny. Don't you like bunnies?"

Tom said, "Well, I guess bunnies are cute. But I'm not a bunny. I'm a man. A bald man."

Lisa said, "But bald men can wear hats with ears too. It's fun. And it's a surprise. The pizza man told me you like surprises. He said you always order the same pizza. So I wanted to give you something different. Something special. Please try it on. Please."

Tom looked at Lisa. She looked very nice and friendly. She looked like she really wanted him to wear the hat. He felt sorry for her. He said, "Okay, okay. I'll try it on. But only for a minute."

He took the hat from Lisa and put it on his head. He felt the ears tickle his cheeks. He looked in the mirror. He saw a bald man with a hat with ears. He looked silly. He laughed. Lisa laughed too.

She said, "You look great, Tom. You look happy. I'm glad you like the hat. And the pizza. Can I come in and have a slice with you?"

Tom said, "Sure, Lisa. Come in. You're very kind. And you make good pizza. And hats. Maybe you can teach me how to make hats with ears too."

Lisa said, "I'd love to, Tom. Maybe we can be friends. And maybe you can order something different next time. Like pepperoni. Or mushrooms. Or pineapple."

Tom said, "Maybe, Lisa. Maybe. But I still like cheese and ham. And I still like surprises. Like you. And your hat."

They smiled at each other and went inside. They ate pizza and talked and laughed. They had a good time. And they wore their hats with ears. The end.

Lily wanted to be a fairy for the party. She had a dress, a wand and a crown. But she needed wings. She asked her mom to help her make some.

"Mom, can we make fairy wings?" Lily said.

"Sure, honey. We need some paper, some glue and some glitter. And we need to measure your arms," Mom said.

Mom got a big sheet of paper and a ruler. She put the ruler on Lily's arm and made a mark. Then she did the same for the other arm.

"Good. Now we can cut out the shape of the wings," Mom said. She folded the paper in half and cut along the mark. She opened the paper and showed Lily.

"Wow, they look like wings!" Lily said.

"Yes, they do. But they need some glue and glitter to make them shiny and light," Mom said. She got a bottle of glue and a jar of glitter. She squeezed some glue on the paper and sprinkled some glitter on top. She did the same for the other wing.

"Can I help?" Lily asked.

"Of course. You can spread the glue and glitter with your fingers. Be careful, it's sticky," Mom said.

Lily and Mom worked together to make the wings sparkle. Then they waited for them to dry.

"Are they ready?" Lily asked.

"Almost. We just need to attach them to your dress. We can use some tape or some pins," Mom said.

She got some tape and some pins and fixed the wings to the back of Lily's dress.

"Done. You look like a beautiful fairy, Lily," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. I love my costume. Can I try it on?" Lily said.

"Sure. Let me help you," Mom said.

She helped Lily put on her dress, her wand and her crown. Then she lifted her up and spun her around.

"You're flying, Lily. You're flying like a fairy," Mom said.

Lily giggled and waved her wand. She felt happy and light. She couldn't wait to show her friends her costume.

She knocked over a glass of water and spilled it on the telephone. The telephone made a loud noise and stopped working.

But her mom did find her. She saw the wet telephone and the broken glass. She was not happy. She looked under the bed and saw Lily. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You ruined my telephone. How can I talk to your dad now?"

Lily felt bad. She came out from under the bed and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to play with the telephone, but I was clumsy. I didn't mean to break it. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom sighed. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm not mad at you, Lily. I'm just disappointed. You should not touch things that are not yours. You should ask before you play with something. You should be more careful and responsible. Do you understand?"

They went to the mom's room and called dad. He was happy to hear from them. He told them he missed them and loved them. They told him they missed him and loved him too. They had a nice chat and said goodbye.

The gray cat looked at Tom and then at Lily. It meowed again and jumped off the branch. It ran away from the tree. Lily was surprised and scared. She came out from behind the tree and said, "Tom, you found me. But why did the kitty run away? I thought it was my friend."

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to visit their grandma every week. Grandma lived in a big house with a garden and a fireplace. She always had cookies and stories for them.

One day, when they were visiting, a storm came. It was very loud and dark outside. Lily and Ben were frightened. They hugged grandma and asked her what to do.

"Don't worry, my dears," grandma said. "We can stay inside and be cozy. Let's light the fireplace and read some books."

Grandma took some wood and matches and went to the fireplace. She put the wood inside and struck a match. A spark flew out and landed on the rug. The rug started to burn.

"Fire! Fire!" grandma shouted. "Lily, Ben, get out of the house!"

Lily and Ben ran to the door. They saw the fire spreading on the rug and the curtains. They were very scared. They wanted to help grandma, but they didn't know how.

"Grandma, come with us!" Lily cried.

"I'm coming, I'm coming!" grandma said. She grabbed a blanket and threw it over the fire. She tried to smother it, but it was too big and hot.

She coughed and ran to the door. She joined Lily and Ben outside. They hugged each other and watched the fire. They heard sirens and saw firemen coming. The firemen put out the fire and checked the house.

"Are you all right?" one of them asked grandma.

"Yes, thank you," grandma said. "But my house is ruined."

"I'm sorry, ma'am," the fireman said. "It was an accident. The spark from the match was too close to the rug. You should always be careful with fire."

Grandma nodded. She looked at Lily and Ben. They had tears in their eyes.

"I'm sorry, grandma," Lily said. "We wanted to have fun with you."

"It's not your fault, my dears," grandma said. "You did the right thing by getting out of the house. Fire is dangerous. You should never play with it or go near it. Do you understand?"

"Yes, grandma," Lily and Ben said.

Grandma hugged them and kissed them. She smiled and said, "Don't worry. We still have each other. And we can always visit another place. Maybe a place with no fireplace."

Lily and Ben smiled and nodded. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful with fire and to love their grandma.

One day, a big bear and a small bee were walking in the forest. The bear liked honey very much, and the bee knew where to find it. The bee said to the bear, "I can show you a tree with honey, but you have to be nice to me and my friends. We work hard to make honey, and we don't like when someone takes it all."

The bear agreed, and followed the bee to the tree. The bee flew to a hole in the trunk, and said, "Here is the honey. You can have some, but not too much. And be careful, there are other bees inside who will sting you if you hurt them."

The bear nodded, and reached his paw into the hole. He scooped out some honey, and licked it. It was sweet and sticky, and he wanted more. He forgot what the bee said, and pushed his paw deeper into the hole. He felt a sharp pain, and pulled his paw out. It was covered with angry bees, who stung him all over. He roared, and ran away from the tree.

The bee flew after him, and said, "Why did you do that? I told you to be nice, and not to take too much. You were greedy, and you made the bees angry. They were only trying to protect their honey, and their home. You should have listened to me, and respected them."

The bear felt sorry, and said, "You are right, I was greedy, and I did not listen. I should have respected you and your friends. You are small, but you are strong, and you work hard. I am sorry for hurting you and your honey. Can you forgive me?"

The bee said, "I can forgive you, but you have to promise me to be more careful, and more kind, next time. Honey is good, but friendship is better. And friendship needs trust, and respect."

The bear promised, and thanked the bee. They became friends, and shared the honey, and the forest. They learned to protect each other, and to value their differences. And they lived happily ever after.

But the book was not gentle. It was loud and scary. It made noises like a dragon. It said, "Roar! I am the king of the castle. You cannot read me. Go away!"

Anna was afraid. She dropped the book and ran to her mom. She said, "Mom, there is a mean book in my bookcase. It roared at me. It hurt my ears."

Mom hugged Anna and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. It is not a mean book. It is a magic book. It can talk and make sounds. It is a book for older kids. I borrowed it from the library for your brother. He likes dragons and castles. But you don't have to read it if you don't like it. You can choose another book from your bookcase. A gentle book. A book that makes you happy."

Anna nodded and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can you help me find a gentle book?"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, I can. Let's go back to your bookcase and settle down with a nice book. Maybe a book about animals or fairies or rainbows. What do you think?"

Anna smiled and said, "Yes, mom. I think that sounds good. I like animals and fairies and rainbows. And I like reading books with you."

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks of different colors and sizes. Some are made of plastic and some are made of steel.

One day, Mom says, "Boys, it is time to organize your toys. You have to put them in the right boxes. Plastic toys go in the blue box and steel toys go in the red box. Can you do that?"

Tom and Sam nod and say, "Yes, Mom, we can do that." They start to sort their toys. Tom picks up a big steel truck. He says, "This is my favorite truck. It is mighty and strong. It can carry anything." He puts it in the red box.

Sam picks up a small plastic car. He says, "This is my favorite car. It is fast and shiny. It can race anyone." He puts it in the blue box.

They keep sorting their toys until they are done. They look at their boxes and smile. They say, "We did it, Mom. We organized our toys. Now we can play with them again."

Mom comes and sees their boxes. She says, "Good job, boys. You are very smart and helpful. I am proud of you. Now you can play with your toys, but remember to put them back in the boxes when you are done."

Tom and Sam hug Mom and say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you." They take out their toys and start to play. They have fun with their plastic and steel toys. They are happy brothers.

Sam and Lily were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run around. But sometimes Sam was not nice to Lily. He liked to tease her and make her sad. He would say mean things, pull her hair and hide her toys.

One day, Sam and Lily found a big bag of salt in the park. Sam had an idea. He wanted to trick Lily and make her cry. He told Lily that the salt was sugar and that they could make a cake with it. Lily believed him and was happy. She loved cake.

They went to Sam's house and mixed the salt with some water and flour. Sam pretended to taste it and said it was yummy. He gave Lily a big spoonful and told her to try it. Lily put the spoon in her mouth and spat it out. It was very salty and bitter. She felt sick and started to cry.

Sam laughed and laughed. He said he was smarter than Lily and that she was silly and stupid. He said he did not want to be her friend anymore. He told her to go away and never come back.

Lily ran out of the house and went home. She was very sad and hurt. She told her mom what happened and her mom hugged her and said she was sorry. She said Sam was not a good friend and that he was rude and mean. She said Lily was a good and humble girl and that she would find better friends who would be kind and honest.

Sam stayed in his house and ate some of the salty cake. He thought he was clever and funny. But soon he felt sick too. His mouth was dry and his stomach was sore. He wanted some water but there was none. He wanted his mom but she was not there. He was alone and scared. He wished he had not teased Lily and that he had been a good friend. He realized he was not smarter than Lily and that he was silly and stupid. He cried and cried but no one heard him. He was very sorry but it was too late.

One day, it was her birthday. She was very happy and excited. She wore a new dress and a ribbon in her hair. She invited her friends to her house for a party. They played games, ate cake and sang songs. Anna received many gifts from her friends. She opened them one by one and said thank you.

Lila liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna was a model doll. She had long hair, pretty clothes and thin legs. Lila wanted to be like Anna when she grew up.

One day, Lila and Anna were having a tea party in Lila's room. Lila poured some water in the cups and pretended it was tea. She gave one cup to Anna and one to herself. She said, "Cheers, Anna! You are the best model in the world!"

Anna did not say anything. She just smiled with her painted lips. Lila did not mind. She liked to talk for both of them. She said, "Anna, do you like tea? I do. It is yummy. But you have to be careful. Too much tea can make you fat. And models have to be thin, right?"

Anna still did not say anything. She just nodded with her plastic head. Lila did not notice. She said, "Anna, do you know what I want to be when I grow up? I want to be a model like you. I want to wear beautiful clothes and walk on the stage and make everyone happy. Do you think I can do that?"

Anna finally said something. She said, "Of course you can, Lila. You are smart and kind and pretty. You can be anything you want. But you know what? Being a model is not the most important thing in life. There are other things that matter more. Like being healthy and happy and having friends and family who love you. And having fun and learning new things and being yourself. Don't you agree?"

Lila was surprised. She had never heard Anna talk so much. She thought about what Anna said. She said, "You are right, Anna. Being a model is not the most important thing in life. There are other things that matter more. Like being healthy and happy and having friends and family who love me. And having fun and learning new things and being myself. I agree with you, Anna. You are the best friend in the world!"

Anna smiled with her painted lips. She said, "You are welcome, Lila. You are the best friend in the world, too. Now, let's finish our tea and then go to sleep. We have a big day tomorrow. We can play more games and have more adventures. Good night, Lila."

Lila hugged Anna and said, "Good night, Anna. I love you." She put Anna next to her pillow and closed her eyes. She felt happy and sleepy. She dreamed of being a model and a doctor and a teacher and a princess and a superhero and a dancer and a singer and a writer and a chef and a painter and a scientist and a farmer and a pilot and a astronaut and a explorer and a friend. She dreamed of being herself.

One day, a little lion was playing with his friends in the grass. He liked to run and jump and roar with them. He wanted to be the fastest and the loudest of all the lions.

But he had a problem. He could not move his tail very well. His tail was short and stiff and did not swing like the other lions' tails. He felt embarrassed and sad. He thought the other lions would laugh at him.

He tried to hide his tail behind his legs or under a bush. But his friends noticed and asked him, "Why do you hide your tail? Is something wrong with it?"

The little lion did not want to tell them the truth. He was afraid they would not like him anymore. He made up a story and said, "My tail is very special. It is a magic tail. It can do things that no other tail can do."

"Like what?" his friends asked, curious.

The little lion thought hard. He wanted to impress them with his magic tail. He said, "My tail can... can... make the sun shine brighter!"

He lifted his tail and pointed it at the sky. He hoped the sun would shine brighter. But nothing happened. The sun stayed the same.

His friends looked at him and said, "That is not magic. That is silly. You are lying to us. Your tail cannot do anything. You are just embarrassed of your tail."

The little lion felt ashamed. He knew he had lied to his friends. He did not want to lose them. He said, "I'm sorry. I lied to you. My tail is not magic. It is just different. I can't move it very well. I was embarrassed of my tail. But I still want to be your friend. Can you forgive me?"

His friends looked at him and smiled. They said, "Of course we can forgive you. We are your friends. We don't care about your tail. We care about you. You are a good lion. You don't need a magic tail to be special. You are special just the way you are."

The little lion felt happy. He hugged his friends and thanked them. He learned to accept his tail and to be honest with his friends. He realized that his tail was not a problem, but a part of him. He was proud of his tail and of himself. He moved his tail as much as he could and joined his friends in the grass. He ran and jumped and roared with them. He was the happiest lion of all.

"Let's go inside, Tom," Sam said. "It is not safe to play in a storm."

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to keep playing with the ball. He ran after it and kicked it hard. The ball flew far away and landed in the street.

"I will get it," Tom said. He did not look both ways. He did not see the big car coming fast. He stepped into the street and ran after the ball.

Sam saw the car and screamed. "Tom, stop! Car!" But it was too late. The car hit Tom and made a loud bang. Tom fell down and did not move. The ball rolled away.

Sam ran to Tom and cried. He was scared and sad. He wanted to help Tom, but he did not know how. The car stopped and the driver got out. He was angry and scared too. He yelled at Sam and Tom. He said they were bad and stupid. He said they should not play in the street.

Sam felt ashamed. He wished he had made Tom listen. He wished he had gone inside with him. He wished he had not played in the storm. He wished Tom was okay. But he knew it was too late. He had lost his brother and his ball. He had made a big mistake. He was sorry, but sorry was not enough.

One day, they see a big zebra lying on the grass. It looks like a tasty meal. They run towards it, hoping to get there before anyone else.

"Give us some meat!" Tim says. "We are hungry too!"

"No!" the lioness says. "This is my meat! You are not strong enough to fight me. You are helpless. Go find your own meat!"

Tim and Sam are scared of the lioness. She has sharp teeth and claws, and she is very fast. They know they cannot win. They yield to her, and run away.

They feel sad and angry. They still want meat, but they do not know where to find it. They wish they were stronger and smarter, like the lioness. They wish they had a pride to help them. They wish they were not helpless.

She tried to write her name, but the chalk broke in her hand. She dropped the pieces and looked at the teacher. The teacher smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily. You can try again."

The teacher walked to Lily and gave her a hug. She said, "Lily, it's okay to cry. Sometimes we cry when we feel anxious or frustrated. But crying does not make the problem go away. You can write your name on the blackboard, Lily. You are a smart and brave girl. You just need to practice and be patient. Do you want to try again with me?"

Lily and Ben helped dad mix the ingredients and pour the batter into the pan. Then dad put the pan in the oven.

"Wow, it looks great!" Lily said.

But one day, Lily was not nice at the library. She saw a book that she wanted very much. It had a big red truck on the cover. She grabbed the book from the shelf and ran to her mom. She said, "I want this book! I want it now!"

Her mom said, "Lily, you have to wait your turn. That book belongs to the library. You have to share it with the other kids. You can borrow it for a few days, but you have to give it back."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She said, "No! It is my book! I will not share it! I will not give it back!" She screamed and cried and kicked. She made a lot of noise. She made the other kids and the nice lady and her mom very sad.

Her mom was very angry. She said, "Lily, you are being very rude and selfish. You are not acting like a big girl. You are acting like a baby. You should be ashamed of yourself. You have to say sorry to the library and to the other kids. And you have to put the book back where you found it."

Lily felt very bad. She knew she was wrong. She said sorry to the library and to the other kids. She put the book back on the shelf. She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. I am sorry I was bad. I will be good next time."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. I am glad you are sorry. I hope you learned your lesson. You can still borrow a book from the library, but you have to be polite and respectful. And you have to remember to say please and thank you."

Lily nodded and said, "I will, mom. I will." She picked another book that she liked. It had a cute bunny on the cover. She said, "Please, mom, can I borrow this book?"

Her mom said, "Yes, you can, Lily. That is a nice book. You can read it with me at home. But first, you have to say thank you to the library."

Lily said, "Thank you, library, for letting me borrow this book. You are very kind and generous. I will take good care of it and I will give it back soon."

The nice lady smiled and said, "You are very welcome, Lily. I am happy you like the book. I hope you enjoy it. And I hope you come back to the library again. You are a good girl."

Bella and Max were playing with their toy box. They liked to pretend they were pirates and find treasure. They put on hats and scarves and looked for shiny things.

"Look, Max, I found a feather!" Bella said, holding up a white and fluffy feather. "Maybe it belongs to a parrot!"

"Wow, let me see!" Max said, reaching for the feather. He took it from Bella and rubbed it on his nose. "It's so soft and tickly!"

But then, Max felt a funny feeling in his nose. He tried to stop it, but he couldn't. He sneezed very loud and hard. The feather flew out of his hand and landed on the floor.

"Achoo!" Max sneezed.

"Bless you!" Bella said. "Are you okay?"

Max nodded, but he looked sad. He liked the feather and wanted to keep it. He looked for it on the floor, but he couldn't find it. He thought it was gone forever.

"Where did it go?" Max asked. "I want it back!"

Bella looked around too, but she didn't see the feather. She saw something else, though. She saw their cat, Fluffy, sitting on the couch. Fluffy had a big smile on his face and something white in his mouth.

"Fluffy!" Bella shouted. "Did you take our feather?"

Fluffy looked at Bella and Max and opened his mouth. The feather fell out and landed on his paw. He licked his lips and purred.

"Bad Fluffy!" Max said. "That was our feather! Give it back!"

But Fluffy didn't listen. He thought the feather was a harmless toy and a tasty snack. He picked it up again and ran away.

Bella and Max chased after him, but he was too fast. He hid under the bed and played with the feather.

Bella and Max were very angry and sad. They wanted their feather back, but they couldn't get it. They decided to find another treasure and play with that instead.

But they never forgot the feather and how Fluffy stole it from them. They learned to be careful with their toys and not let Fluffy near them. They also learned to say "achoo" when they sneezed, because sneezing can make things fly away.

Lily liked to eat cauliflower. She liked how it was white and soft and good for her. But her brother Tom did not like cauliflower. He said it was yucky and boring and he only wanted to eat candy.

One day, Mom made cauliflower for dinner. She put cheese on top and baked it in the oven. It smelled yummy and Lily was happy. But Tom was not happy. He said he would not eat it and he threw a tantrum. He said he wanted candy instead.

Mom was sad and angry. She said Tom was being ignorant. She said he did not know how good cauliflower was and he was missing out. She said he could not have candy if he did not eat his dinner. She said candy was bad for him and it would make his teeth rot and his tummy ache.

Tom did not listen. He ran to his room and slammed the door. He found his secret stash of candy and started to eat it. He thought he was smart and he did not need cauliflower. He thought he was happy and he did not need Mom.

But he was wrong. The candy was too sweet and too much. It made his teeth hurt and his tummy ache. He felt sick and he wanted to cry. He wished he had eaten the cauliflower instead. He wished he had listened to Mom.

He went to the kitchen and saw Lily and Mom eating the cauliflower. It looked warm and cheesy and delicious. He saw that Lily and Mom were smiling and talking and having fun. He felt cold and lonely and sad.

He said he was sorry. He said he was ignorant and he wanted to try the cauliflower. He said he did not want any more candy and he wanted to be with Mom.

Mom hugged him and said she forgave him. She said she loved him and she wanted him to be healthy and happy. She gave him a plate of cauliflower and said he could have a little candy later if he ate it.

Tom ate the cauliflower and he liked it. He said it was not yucky or boring. He said it was white and soft and good for him. He said he was glad he ate it and he thanked Mom.

He learned a lesson. He learned that he should not be ignorant and he should try new things. He learned that he should listen to Mom and he should eat his vegetables. He learned that candy was not everything and he should not eat too much. He learned that cauliflower was better than candy.

Lily and Ben were brother and sister. They liked to play with their toy cars and trucks. They pretended to drive them on the road, in the park, and in the garage. Sometimes they made noises like honk, beep, and vroom.

One day, they decided to drive their toy cars to their friend's house. They packed their cars in a bag and walked with their mom. On the way, they saw a big house with a fence and a gate. The house looked old and sad. The windows were broken and the paint was peeling. The grass was dry and the flowers were wilted.

"Mom, what is that house?" Lily asked.

"That is a troubled house, Lily. It means that the people who live there have many problems and no one helps them. They are unhappy and lonely," Mom said.

"Can we help them, Mom?" Ben asked.

Mom smiled and said, "That is very kind of you, Ben. But we don't know them and they might not want our help. Sometimes the best way to help troubled people is to pray for them and wish them well."

Lily and Ben nodded. They felt sorry for the troubled house and the people inside. They said a silent prayer and wished them peace and joy. Then they continued to walk to their friend's house, where they had a lot of fun playing with their toy cars and trucks.

The moral of the story is: We should be compassionate and respectful to people who are troubled, even if we don't know them or can't help them directly. We should also be grateful for what we have and enjoy our friends and family.

Sara and Ben were twins who loved to play in the park. One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It was white and shiny and had a flag on it.

"Wow, look at that boat!" Sara said. "It is so pretty!"

"That is not a boat, Sara. That is a yacht," Ben said. He was gifted at learning new words. "A yacht is a big boat that rich people have."

"Can we go on the yacht, Ben?" Sara asked.

"No, Sara. We can't go on the yacht. It is not ours. We have to ask first," Ben said.

But Sara did not listen. She ran to the yacht and climbed on it. She saw a man sitting on a chair. He was reading a book and drinking a cup.

"Hello, mister!" Sara said. "Can I play on your yacht?"

The man looked up and saw Sara. He was angry. He did not like children on his yacht.

"Hey, get off my yacht, you little brat!" he shouted. "You are making it dirty with your shoes!"

He grabbed a cloth and tried to wipe the dirt off his yacht. But Sara did not want to leave. She liked the yacht. She saw a big wheel and a horn.

"Look, Ben, I can drive the yacht!" she said. She turned the wheel and pressed the horn. The yacht made a loud noise and moved a little.

"Stop it, stop it, stop it!" the man yelled. "You are ruining my yacht!"

Ben ran to the yacht and tried to get Sara off. He was scared. He did not want to get in trouble.

"Sara, come on, we have to go!" he said. "The man is mad at us!"

But Sara did not want to go. She wanted to play more. She saw a rope and a bucket.

"Look, Ben, I can fish on the yacht!" she said. She threw the rope and the bucket into the water. The bucket filled with water and sank.

"Stop it, stop it, stop it!" the man screamed. "You are sinking my yacht!"

He jumped off his chair and ran to the rope. He tried to pull the bucket up. But it was too heavy. He fell into the water.

Sara and Ben saw the man in the water. They were shocked. They did not mean to make him fall.

"Sorry, mister!" they said. "We were just playing!"

They ran off the yacht and back to the park. They did not want to see the man again.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned not to go on other people's yachts without asking. They learned that yachts are not toys. They learned that some people are not nice.

Red socks matched with red socks. Blue socks matched with blue socks. Green socks matched with green socks. Yellow socks matched with yellow socks. Amy was happy. She finished her easy job for the week. Now, she could go play with her friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat fruit. His favorite fruit was the original red apple. Every day, Tim would go to the market with his mom to buy some fruit.

One day, Tim saw a big, green fruit at the market. He had never seen this fruit before. He wanted to try it, but his mom said, "No, Tim. You should ignore that fruit. We don't know if it's good or bad." But Tim didn't listen to his mom. He took the green fruit and hid it in his bag.

When they got home, Tim went to his room and ate the green fruit. It tasted very bad. After a while, Tim felt sick. His tummy hurt a lot. His mom found out about the green fruit and was very sad. Tim should have listened to his mom and ignored the green fruit. Now, he was sick and unhappy.

One day, a happy boy named Tim went to the shore with his mom. Tim was very enthusiastic. He loved to play in the sand and listen to the big waves. Tim's mom said, "Be careful, Tim. Don't go too close to the water."

Tim liked to imagine he was a big, strong pirate looking for treasure. He found a big stick and pretended it was his pirate sword. Tim played and played in the sand, but he didn't listen to his mom. He went closer and closer to the water.

A big wave came and took Tim's stick away. Tim was sad and scared. His mom was right. Tim should have listened to her. Now, his pirate sword was gone, and he couldn't play anymore.

When they got to grandma's house, Lucy showed her fan to grandma. Grandma was happy to see it. They all sat together in the living room, and the fan kept them cool while the sun was harsh outside. They had a wonderful day, and Lucy was glad she brought her fan with her.

Tim, his mom, and Buddy walked around the neighborhood. They asked people if they knew Buddy. Finally, they found Buddy's owner. The owner was happy to see Buddy again. Remy did not want to listen to Bella. He wanted to keep playing. But Bella knew she had to prevent Remy from falling in the water. So, Bella flew up and grabbed Remy's antler with her beak. She pulled him away from the river, just in time.

Remy was happy that Bella saved him. He said, "Thank you, Bella. You are a good friend." From that day on, Remy was more careful when playing near the big river. And even though he was still a dizzy reindeer, he knew that his friends would always help him stay safe.

One of the reindeer answered, "Of course, little girl! What do you want to collect?"

Lily looked around and saw some fallen antlers on the ground. "I want to collect these antlers. They are so pretty!" she said.

The reindeer smiled and said, "Sure, take them! We don't need them anymore." 

Lily was so happy to collect the antlers. She thanked the reindeer and went back home to show her impressive collection to her family.

But one night, there was a big storm. The wind blew and the rain fell hard. Lily was scared, but Spot stayed by her side. He jumped onto the new mattress and cuddled with Lily, making her feel safe. The storm went away, and they both fell asleep on the mattress.

In the morning, Spot realized that the new mattress was not so bad after all. It was soft and warm, and it was a good place to sleep. He didn't hate it anymore.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, we may not like something new at first, but if we give it a chance, we might find that it's not so bad after all.

Lily was a little cat who liked to play with her ball. She would roll it, chase it, and catch it with her paws. She was very good at playing with her ball, and she wanted to improve. She wanted to be the best ball player in the world.

One day, she saw a big dog playing with a bigger ball. The dog was fast and strong, and he could throw the ball very far. Lily thought the dog was amazing, and she wanted to play with him. She ran to the dog and said, "Hi, I am Lily. Can I play with you and your ball?"

The dog looked at Lily and laughed. He said, "No, you can't. You are too small and slow. You can't play with my ball. It is too big and heavy for you. Go away, little cat. You are not good enough."

Bob said, "Don't listen to him. He is a bully. He thinks he is better than everyone else. He is not. You are not too small and slow. You are not a bad ball player. You are a good cat. Once upon a time, there was a happy little mouse. He liked to whistle a song and march around the house. He always hummed his happy tune each and every day. As he skipped and hopped, passersby would watch him play. 

One day, the little mouse came across a button lying on the ground. It had a bright green color and shined like the sun. He picked up the button, and with a toothy grin he brushed it off, and gave it a little spin. 

At once, the little mouse began to whistle a happy jig. He danced around and around, twirling the button in a big ol'wig. He laughed with joy and seemed to really have fun, as passersby whispered with bright smiles,"Look! That's one fun mouse!" 

From that moment, the happy little mouse would often skip by whistling a sweet tune and twirling the button which held it's green hue. 

The end.

The mineral learned that being patient can help us stay safe. The mineral went back to the forest and told the tree about its adventure. The tree was proud of the mineral for being brave and patient. The mineral was happy to be back home.

His dad said, "It's okay. Sometimes we don't get the answers right away. That's why it's important to be patient and listen more than you talk." He gave Benny another sign.

Benny nodded. He knew he had been a little too bossy. From then on he tried to be quieter and make sure he was really taking time to listen to others before trying to answer questions.

As the sun started to set, Lily and Olive went back inside. Lily's mom asked how her day was. Lily said it was brilliant because she got to play with Olive and Olive made her feel better when she fell down. Lily loved Olive so much and knew that Olive loved her too.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why did you put a rock in the pot? You could have burned the house or hurt yourself!"

"That was not a mineral, that was a piece of coal," she said. "It is not good for cooking or eating. It is only good for making fire or drawing. You should not play with things you do not know. You should ask me or Dad first."

Tom and Sue nodded and apologized. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with their toys instead of rocks. They also decided to listen to Mom and Dad more. They knew they loved them and wanted them to be safe and happy.

They said, "Bye, zebra! See you next time!"

Lily and Max were playing by the river. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. Sometimes they saw fish or ducks or frogs. But today they saw something new. It was an otter.

The otter was brown and furry and had a long tail. It swam fast and dived under the water. Then it popped up again and looked at Lily and Max. It made a funny noise, like a snort.

"Hello, otter!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The otter snorted again and nodded. It swam closer to the shore and took a stone in its mouth. Then it threw it back into the water with a splash.

"Wow, you are good at throwing stones!" Max said. "Can we try?"

The otter nodded again and gave them another stone. Lily and Max threw their stones and tried to make bigger splashes than the otter. They laughed and clapped and had fun.

But then they heard a loud roar. It came from the other side of the river. It was an enormous bear. The bear was hungry and angry and wanted to eat the otter.

"Run, otter, run!" Lily and Max shouted. "The bear is coming!"

The otter heard them and saw the bear. It was scared and had to decide what to do. It could swim away or hide under the water or fight the bear. But it did not want to leave Lily and Max. They were its new friends.

So the otter decided to be brave. It snorted and bared its teeth and faced the bear. It threw a stone at the bear's nose and made it sneeze. Then it threw another stone at the bear's eye and made it blink. Then it threw a third stone at the bear's ear and made it howl.

The bear was surprised and hurt and angry. It did not like the otter's stones. It decided to give up and go away. It roared and turned around and ran back to the woods.

Lily and Max cheered and clapped and hugged the otter. They were proud and happy and grateful. The otter had saved them from the bear.

"Thank you, otter, thank you!" Lily and Max said. "You are very brave and smart and kind. You are our hero!"

The otter smiled and snorted and hugged them back. It was glad and happy and thankful. Lily and Max were its friends.

One day, a farmer was working hard in his field. He was planting seeds and watering them. He wanted to grow many fruits and vegetables for his family and the market. He also brought him some books and toys for his children. The farmer was grateful for his friend's support. He liked to talk to him and learn new things.

One time, the doctor asked the farmer if he wanted to see his clinic. The clinic was in the town, which was far from the field. The farmer had never been to the town before. He was curious and excited, but also a little scared. He agreed to go with the doctor.

The farmer was amazed by the doctor's work, but he also felt uncomfortable. He did not understand everything he saw and heard. He missed his field and his family. He told the doctor that he wanted to go back. The doctor understood and smiled. He drove him back to his field and hugged him goodbye. Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and balls. But they do not like the same food. Tom likes steak, but Sam hates steak. Sam likes cheese, but Tom hates cheese.

One day, Mom makes steak and cheese for dinner. She puts them on two blue plates. She gives one plate to Tom and one plate to Sam. She says, "Eat your dinner, boys. It is good for you."

Tom is happy. He picks up his fork and knife. He cuts his steak and eats it. He says, "Mmm, this steak is yummy. Thank you, Mom."

Sam is sad. He looks at his plate. He sees the steak and the cheese. He says, "Yuck, this steak is icky. I do not want it. I want cheese only."

Mom says, "No, Sam. You have to eat some steak. It has protein. It makes you strong."

Sam says, "No, Mom. I hate steak. It is gross. It makes me sick."

Tom says, "Sam, you are silly. Steak is good. You should try it. Maybe you will like it."

Sam says, "No, Tom. You are silly. Cheese is good. You should try it. Maybe you will like it."

Tom and Sam start to argue. They say, "Steak is better!" "No, cheese is better!" They raise their voices. They make a lot of noise.

Mom says, "Stop, boys. Stop fighting. You are making a mess. You are wasting your food. You are hurting my ears."

Tom and Sam look at Mom. They see her angry face. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom."

Lila and Max liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. Lila's favorite car was a red one that could zoom very fast. Max's favorite car was a blue one that had thick wheels and could go over bumps.

One day, they decided to have a race with their cars. They made a track with some books and boxes. They put a sticker at the end of the track to show who would win. They agreed on the rules: no pushing, no cheating, no crying.

"Are you ready?" Lila asked Max.

"Yes, I am ready," Max said. "My car is better than yours. It can go over anything."

"That's your opinion," Lila said. "My car is faster than yours. It can zoom like a rocket."

They counted to three and started the race. Their cars zoomed along the track, passing the books and boxes. Lila's car was ahead of Max's car, but Max's car was catching up. They both wanted to win.

But then, something happened. Lila's car zoomed too fast and hit a box. The box fell over and blocked the track. Max's car could not go over the box. It crashed into the box and stopped.

Lila and Max looked at their cars. They were both stuck. They looked at each other. They did not know what to do.

Then, they started to laugh. They realized that it was just a game. They did not care who won. They picked up their cars and hugged each other.

"Your car is very fast," Max said.

"Your car has very thick wheels," Lila said.

They decided to share their cars and play together. They had more fun that way. They learned that it was not important to have the best car, but to have a good friend.

One day, they saw a big slide in the park. They both ran to it and tried to climb up. But the slide was too high and slippery for them. They slid down and bumped their heads. They cried and rubbed their heads.

Mom came and hugged them. She said, "You two are selfish. You should share your toys and help each other. Then you can have more fun and make more friends. Now you have hurt your heads and you need to rest."

She took them to a bench and gave them some water and salad. She said, "Salad is good for you. It has green leaves and red tomatoes and yellow cheese. It makes you strong and healthy. You should eat some and say sorry to each other."

Lily and Ben looked at the salad. They did not like salad. They liked candy and cake and ice cream. They made faces and pushed the salad away. They said, "No, we don't want salad. We want candy and cake and ice cream."

Mom shook her head and said, "You two are selfish. You should eat what is good for you and not what you want. Candy and cake and ice cream are bad for you. They make you sick and fat and unhappy. You should eat some salad and say thank you to me."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They saw that they were both selfish and rude. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Ben. We will eat some salad and share our toys and help each other. We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good. I love you, too. Now eat some salad and rest. Then you can play again and have more fun and make more friends."

"Are you sick?" Lily asked.

"Yes, I have to go to the hospital soon. The doctor said I have a bad bug in my blood," Sam said.

Lily and Tom felt sorry for Sam. They wanted to help him.

"We have an idea. Why don't you listen to the sounds of the park with us? Maybe they will make you feel better," Tom said.

Sam smiled a little. "Okay, I will try."

Lily and Tom learned that sometimes, the best way to make someone happy is to observe them and listen to them. They also learned that sounds can be beautiful and soothing. They became friends with Sam and hoped he would get well soon.

Sam was not sure. He thought the board looked old and dangerous. He saw some holes and cracks on it. He said, "No, Ben, that is a bad idea. The board might break and hurt us. Let's play somewhere else."

But Ben did not listen. He was foolish and wanted to have fun. He said, "Don't be scared, Sam. It will be fun. Watch me!" He took his car and ran to the board. He knelt down and pushed his car hard. The car zoomed on the board and flew in the air.

But then, something bad happened. The board snapped in half and one of the nails pierced Ben's hand. Ben screamed and dropped his car. He felt a lot of pain and blood came out of his hand.

Sam ran to him and saw his wound. He was scared and sorry for his friend. He said, "Ben, Ben, are you okay? I told you it was a bad idea. We need to get help. Come on, let's go to the nurse."

He helped Ben stand up and they walked to the nurse. The nurse cleaned Ben's hand and put a bandage on it. She said, "You were very foolish, Ben. You should not play with things that are old and dangerous. You could have hurt yourself more. Next time, listen to your friend. He was smart and careful."

Ben felt ashamed and sad. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. You were right. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. Will you still be my friend?"

Sam smiled and hugged him. He said, "Of course, Ben. You are still my friend. But next time, let's play with something safe and fun. Okay?"

Ben nodded and smiled back. He said, "Okay, Sam. Thank you for being my friend. And thank you, nurse, for helping me."

The nurse smiled and said, "You're welcome, Ben. Now, go and play nicely. And be careful."

Ben and Sam left the nurse and went back to the park. They played with their balls and had fun. They learned their lesson and never played with the board again.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big pile of leaves and wanted to jump in it. But they had to be careful, because there were some twigs in the leaves that could hurt them.

"Look, Ben, I found a twig!" Anna said, holding a long and thin stick. "I can use it as a sword!"

"Me too, me too!" Ben said, looking for a twig of his own. He saw one that was very short and thick. He picked it up and said, "This is my sword! It is heavy and strong!"

Anna and Ben pretended to be knights and fought with their twigs. They made noises like "clash" and "bang" and "ouch". They had a lot of fun, until Anna hit Ben's hand with her twig.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben yelled, dropping his twig and holding his hand. "That hurt, Anna! You hit me too hard!"

"I'm sorry, Ben, I didn't mean to!" Anna said, feeling bad. "Are you okay?"

Ben looked at his hand and saw a small cut. It was bleeding a little bit. He felt scared and sad. He started to cry.

Anna hugged Ben and said, "Don't cry, Ben, it's okay. I'll get you a band-aid. Come on, let's go to Mommy. She'll make it better."

Anna and Ben ran to their mommy, who was sitting on a bench. She saw their faces and asked, "What happened, my loves?"

Anna and Ben told her what happened. Mommy said, "Oh, poor Ben, let me see your hand. It's not a big cut, but it needs a band-aid. Here, I have one in my bag. There you go, all better. And Anna, you have to be careful when you play with twigs. They can be sharp and hurt someone. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, Mommy, I understand. I'm sorry, Ben. Can we still be friends?"

Ben smiled and said, "Yes, Anna, we can still be friends. I'm sorry I yelled at you. Can we still play?"

Mommy said, "Of course you can still play. But be gentle and kind to each other, okay?"

Anna and Ben said, "Okay, Mommy, we will." They hugged each other and said, "We love you, Mommy."

Mommy said, "I love you too, my sweeties. Now go and have fun, but be careful."

Anna and Ben went back to the pile of leaves. They decided to put their twigs away and play something else. They had a lot of fun, and they didn't yell or hurt each other again. They were happy and good friends.

Lisa loved to play her flute. She could make many sounds with it, like birds, wind, and songs. She practiced every day and got better and better. She was very proud of her flute and her skill.

One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw some other kids playing. She wanted to join them, but they did not have any flutes. They had balls, dolls, cars, and blocks. Lisa thought her flute was better than all those toys. She walked up to them and said, "I have a flute. It is incredible. You should all listen to me play."

The other kids looked at her and shook their heads. They did not want to listen to her flute. They wanted to play with their own toys and have fun. They said, "No, thank you. We are busy. You can play with us if you want, but you have to share your flute."

Lisa did not like that. She did not want to share her flute. She wanted to keep it for herself and show off. She said, "No, I will not share. My flute is mine. You have to do what I say. I demand that you listen to me play."

The other kids did not like that. They did not like her attitude. They did not like her demand. They said, "No, we will not do what you say. You are being rude and bossy. You can play by yourself. We do not want to be your friends."

Lisa was shocked and sad. She did not understand why the other kids did not like her. She did not understand why they did not want to be her friends. She did not understand that she was being selfish and mean. She ran to her mom and cried.

Her mom hugged her and asked her what happened. Lisa told her everything. Her mom listened and nodded. She said, "Lisa, I understand that you love your flute and you are good at it. But you cannot force other people to like what you like. You cannot demand that they do what you want. You have to respect their choices and feelings. You have to be kind and generous. You have to share your flute and your talent. That is how you make friends and have fun."

Lisa thought about what her mom said. She realized that she was wrong. She felt sorry for what she did. She said, "Mom, you are right. I was being bad. I want to say sorry to the other kids. I want to share my flute and play with them. Can we go back to the park?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course we can. I am glad that you learned your lesson. Come on, let's go."

Lisa and her mom went back to the park. Lisa found the other kids and apologized to them. She asked them if they wanted to play with her and her flute. The other kids accepted her apology and agreed to play with her. They took turns with the flute and the other toys. They made sounds and songs and stories. They laughed and had fun. Lisa was happy. She made new friends and learned to share. She realized that her flute was incredible, but so were the other toys and the other kids. She realized that playing together was better than playing alone. She realized that being nice was better than being bossy. She realized that sharing was caring.

Timmy was scared of the dark. He did not like to sleep in his room alone. He had bad dreams that made him cry. He dreamed of big monsters that chased him and wanted to hurt him. He called them nightmares.

One night, he heard a loud noise outside his window. He thought it was a nightmare coming to get him. He hid under his blanket and hoped it would go away. But the noise came again, louder and closer. He peeked out and saw a flash of light and a big cloud. He screamed and ran to his mom and dad's room.

Mom and dad were awake too. They heard the noise and saw the light. They knew it was not a nightmare, but a storm. They hugged Timmy and told him not to be afraid. They said it was just thunder and lightning, and they would not hurt him. They said thunder was the sound of the sky talking, and lightning was the spark of the sky striking.

Timmy was curious. He asked them why the sky was talking and striking. Mom and dad said the sky was angry because it was dirty. It had too much dust and smoke and rain. It wanted to clean itself and make the air fresh. They said the storm was like a big shower for the sky.

Timmy felt better. He liked showers. They made him clean and happy. He wondered if the sky would be happy too after the storm. He asked mom and dad if he could watch the sky shower with them. They said yes, and they took him to the window. They watched the thunder and lightning together, and counted the seconds between them. They told Timmy stories about the sky and the stars and the moon. Timmy forgot his nightmares and smiled. He was not scared of the dark anymore. He was glad he had mom and dad with him. He felt safe and loved. He fell asleep in their arms, dreaming of the sky.

Jill was sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. Mom said she had to stay in bed and take a pill. Jill did not like pills. They were big and bitter and made her gag.

"Please, Jill, you have to take the pill. It will make you feel better," Mom said, holding a glass of water and a pill.

"No, no, no! I don't want it! It's yucky!" Jill said, hiding under the covers.

Mom sighed. She was patient, but she was also worried. She knew Jill needed the pill to fight the germs in her body. She had an idea.

"Jill, do you want to see something cool?" Mom asked.

Jill peeked out from the covers. She was curious.

"What is it?" she asked.

Mom smiled. She put the pill on a spoon and held it over the glass of water.

"Watch this. The pill will rise in the water. It will make bubbles and fizz. It will be like a magic trick," Mom said.

Jill watched as Mom dropped the pill in the water. She saw the pill rise to the top and make a lot of bubbles and fizz. It looked fun.

"Wow! That's cool!" Jill said.

Mom nodded.

"Yes, it is. And you know what? The pill will do the same thing in your tummy. It will rise and make bubbles and fizz and help you get well. Do you want to try it?" Mom asked.

Jill thought about it. She still did not like pills, but she liked bubbles and fizz. She liked magic tricks. She wanted to get well.

"Okay, I'll try it," Jill said.

Mom gave her the glass of water with the pill. Jill held her nose and drank it. She felt the pill rise in her throat and make bubbles and fizz. She made a face, but she swallowed it.

"Good girl, Jill. You did it. I'm proud of you," Mom said, hugging her.

Jill smiled. She felt a little better. She hoped the pill would work its magic in her tummy. She lay down and closed her eyes. Mom kissed her forehead and left the room.

Anna liked to read books. She had many books on her bookshelf. She liked to look at the pictures and learn new words. Sometimes she read to her teddy bear, who listened very well.

One day, Anna found a new book on her bookshelf. It was big and shiny and had a dragon on the cover. Anna loved dragons. She took the book and opened it. She saw many colorful pages with dragons and knights and castles. She wanted to read it right away.

She sat on the floor with her teddy bear and started to read. She read about a brave knight who fought a bad dragon. She read about a princess who was trapped in a tower. She read about a magic sword that could cut through anything. She was so excited that she did not hear her brother come into the room.

Her brother was Tom. He was older than Anna and he liked to tease her. He saw her reading the book and he wanted to take it from her. He walked quietly behind her and grabbed the book. He said, "Ha ha, this is my book now. You can't read it. It's too hard for you."

Anna was very angry. She loved the book and she wanted to finish it. She did not like Tom taking it from her. She shouted, "No, Tom, give it back. It's my book. I found it on my bookshelf. You are mean and rude."

Tom laughed and ran away with the book. He said, "Too bad, Anna. You can't catch me. You are too slow and small. This book is mine and I will keep it."

Anna did not give up. She got up and ran after Tom. She was fast and smart. She saw Tom run into the kitchen. She followed him and saw him hide behind the table. She jumped on him and tried to get the book. They both pulled and pushed and shouted.

Then, Anna did something that surprised Tom. She bit him on the arm. She bit him hard and did not let go. Tom felt a sharp pain and dropped the book. He screamed, "Ow, ow, ow, Anna, stop it. You bit me. That hurts. You are crazy."

Anna let go of his arm and grabbed the book. She said, "That's what you get for taking my book. You deserved it. You are a bad brother. Don't ever touch my bookshelf again."

She ran back to her room with the book and her teddy bear. She closed the door and locked it. She sat on the floor and continued to read. She was happy and proud. She had won the book back and taught Tom a lesson.

Tom went to his mom and showed her his arm. He had a red mark and a small wound. He said, "Mom, mom, look what Anna did. She bit me. She bit me hard. She is serious and mean. She needs a time out."

Mom looked at his arm and frowned. She said, "Tom, what did you do to make Anna bite you? Did you take something from her? Did you tease her? Did you bother her?"

Tom did not answer. He looked down and felt ashamed. He knew he had done something wrong. He knew he had started the fight. He knew he had been mean and rude.

Mom said, "Tom, I think you owe Anna an apology. You should not take things from her without asking. You should not laugh at her or call her names. You should be nice and respectful to your sister. She is your family and you should love her."

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom, you are right. I am sorry. I will say sorry to Anna and give her a hug. I will not take her book again. I will be a good brother."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. I am glad you understand. Now go and make up with Anna. And be careful with your arm. It might get infected. I will put some cream and a bandage on it."

Tom said, "OK, mom, thank you. I love you." He went to Anna's room and knocked on the door. He said, "Anna, Anna, can I come in? I want to say sorry to you. I want to be your friend."

Anna heard his voice and opened the door. She saw his arm and felt sorry for him. She said, "Tom, I am sorry too. I should not have bitten you. That was not nice. I want to be your friend too."

They hugged and said sorry to each other. They smiled and felt happy. They decided to share the book and read it together. They learned about dragons and knights and castles. They had fun and enjoyed the book. They were good siblings and they loved each other.

The little boy was so worried that he went for a walk in the woods. As he was walking, he saw a little squirrel. The boy asked the squirrel for help.

The squirrel said, "If you keep walking, you will find your answer."

The little boy kept walking until he saw a big tree. Climbing up the tree was a big bird. The bird said, "I can help you find your answer. Follow me!"

The bird flew off and the little boy followed. He followed the bird until he reached a meadow. There was a small pond with a bridge in the middle.

The bird said, "Go across the bridge and you'll find your answer."

The little boy crossed the bridge and he saw a big beehive. He heard the buzz of the bees, and he knew he had found his answer.

The little boy was so excited! He had finally found a way to reach his goal. He thanked the bird and the squirrel, then he raced home to tell his mom and dad the good news.

But one day, the worm noticed something strange. Another worm had appeared on the trail. The selfish worm wanted to keep the trail all to himself and be the only one to explore it.

He ran up to the new worm and said, "This trail is mine!" But the new worm just laughed and said, "Oh, no it isn't!"

The selfish worm was so surprised that he fell over in shock. He couldn't believe that someone else wanted to explore the trail too.

But then the new worm helped him up and said, "I think two worms exploring this trail together would be even more exciting! What do you think?"

The selfish worm thought about it, and then he smiled and said, "Yes, I think you're right! Exploring together would be very exciting!" And so the two worms explored the trail together. They even found lots of amazing new things that the selfish worm had never noticed before.

The rabbit thanked the wise owl, and hopped off on his adventure.

Suddenly, the man appeared out of nowhere! He had managed to find a rod and he gave it to her with a smile. She was so happy that she hugged him and they got married.

And they both lived happily ever after - fishing with their rod!

One day, a strong wind came and blew Jasper's cobweb away! The poor spider was so sad!

Jasper was determined to build his cobweb back up. He scrambled up the long vines and worked away spinning out his web. But try as hard as he could, the cobweb would not look how it did before. Until one day, Jasper had an idea. He spooled the strands backwards and when he had finished, he was surprised to find that the cobweb was better than before! He had reversed the cobweb and made it look even more special.

From that day on, Jasper's cobweb was admired by all in the garden, and it became even more rare and beautiful.

He found one toy that was broken, so he didn't let his sister play with it. Timmy was a good big brother and always made sure his sister was safe.
